From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a [dynamic list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Lists#Dynamic_lists "Wikipedia:WikiProject Lists") and may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness. You can help by [editing the page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:EditPage/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents "Special:EditPage/List of association footballers who died after on-field incidents") to add missing items, with references to [reliable sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources").

This is a **list of association footballers who died** due to football-related incidents.

The primary causes of on-field deaths have evolved over time. Improvements in [infection control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infection_control "Infection control") and [emergency surgery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgery "Surgery") since the early days of organised soccer have mostly eliminated the fatal complications that were once common after routine sporting injuries. [Squad rotation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squad_rotation_system "Squad rotation system") and [substitutes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)") have also reduced the need for seriously ill players to start, or remain in, games, and [lifestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifestyle_disease "Lifestyle disease") factors are now tightly controlled.

However, [deaths from heart failure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudden_cardiac_death_of_athletes "Sudden cardiac death of athletes") have increased as the intense pace of the modern game has placed higher demands on players' [aerobic conditioning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerobic_conditioning "Aerobic conditioning"). Following an increase in heart-related deaths,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents#cite_note-deaths_on_field-1) both during matches and training, in 2007 the [International Federation of Association Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA") (FIFA) considered mandatory cardiac testing,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents#cite_note-2) already in place for years in some countries, such as Italy.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents#cite_note-3) By 2009, FIFA pre-competition medical assessment included family history, heart rhythm, sounds, and [electrocardiogram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrocardiogram "Electrocardiogram") results.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents#cite_note-PCMA-4) The [Union of European Football Associations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") (UEFA) required extensive medical tests, including electrocardiogram and [echocardiogram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echocardiogram "Echocardiogram") for players in the Europa League 2011–12.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents#cite_note-UEFA_Europa_Regs-5) Constant monitoring has been advised.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents#cite_note-6)

The _FIFA Sudden Death Report_ (FIFA-SDR) was carried out by [Saarland University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saarland_University "Saarland University") and published in 2020.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents#cite_note-7) The report recorded worldwide deaths attributed to sudden cardiac arrest or other unexplained sudden death while playing (or shortly after playing) football from 2014 to 2018. There were 617 cases during the five-year period. In the majority of cases where an [autopsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autopsy "Autopsy") was carried out, the cause of death was [coronary heart disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronary_heart_disease "Coronary heart disease").

Most non-cardiac deaths are the result of [blunt trauma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blunt_trauma "Blunt trauma") to the head or torso, resulting in life-threatening conditions such as [intracerebral hemorrhage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intracerebral_hemorrhage "Intracerebral hemorrhage") and [peritonitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peritonitis "Peritonitis"), caused by colliding with other players, goalposts or stadium architecture. Challenging another player by targeting their body, an important part of soccer for most of the 20th century, is penalised automatically under modern refereeing guidelines, as is "dangerous play" such as playing the ball with a foot above shoulder height.

As with other forms of outdoor recreation, fatal [lightning strikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightning_injury "Lightning injury") are a rare but persistent problem, especially at training grounds where there is no stadium structure to draw the lightning away.

## List

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: List")]

The list includes players who died either during matches or training, or as the result of incidents during matches or training for various reasons, such as injuries, cardiac arrest, natural death, and sometimes for unknown reasons. Death may occur immediately or several days after the injury or fall, but is still directly attributable to football-related activities.

It does not include players who suffered cardiac "death" on the pitch but were successfully resuscitated and survived, such as [Fabrice Muamba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabrice_Muamba "Fabrice Muamba") and [Christian Eriksen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Eriksen "Christian Eriksen").

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a [dynamic list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Lists#Dynamic_lists "Wikipedia:WikiProject Lists") and may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness. You can help by [editing the page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:EditPage/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents "Special:EditPage/List of association footballers who died after on-field incidents") to add missing items, with references to [reliable sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources").

This is a **list of association footballers who died** due to football-related incidents.

The primary causes of on-field deaths have evolved over time. Improvements in [infection control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infection_control "Infection control") and [emergency surgery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgery "Surgery") since the early days of organised soccer have mostly eliminated the fatal complications that were once common after routine sporting injuries. [Squad rotation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squad_rotation_system "Squad rotation system") and [substitutes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)") have also reduced the need for seriously ill players to start, or remain in, games, and [lifestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifestyle_disease "Lifestyle disease") factors are now tightly controlled.

However, [deaths from heart failure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudden_cardiac_death_of_athletes "Sudden cardiac death of athletes") have increased as the intense pace of the modern game has placed higher demands on players' [aerobic conditioning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerobic_conditioning "Aerobic conditioning"). Following an increase in heart-related deaths,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents#cite_note-deaths_on_field-1) both during matches and training, in 2007 the [International Federation of Association Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA") (FIFA) considered mandatory cardiac testing,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents#cite_note-2) already in place for years in some countries, such as Italy.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents#cite_note-3) By 2009, FIFA pre-competition medical assessment included family history, heart rhythm, sounds, and [electrocardiogram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrocardiogram "Electrocardiogram") results.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents#cite_note-PCMA-4) The [Union of European Football Associations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") (UEFA) required extensive medical tests, including electrocardiogram and [echocardiogram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echocardiogram "Echocardiogram") for players in the Europa League 2011–12.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents#cite_note-UEFA_Europa_Regs-5) Constant monitoring has been advised.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents#cite_note-6)

The _FIFA Sudden Death Report_ (FIFA-SDR) was carried out by [Saarland University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saarland_University "Saarland University") and published in 2020.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents#cite_note-7) The report recorded worldwide deaths attributed to sudden cardiac arrest or other unexplained sudden death while playing (or shortly after playing) football from 2014 to 2018. There were 617 cases during the five-year period. In the majority of cases where an [autopsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autopsy "Autopsy") was carried out, the cause of death was [coronary heart disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronary_heart_disease "Coronary heart disease").

Most non-cardiac deaths are the result of [blunt trauma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blunt_trauma "Blunt trauma") to the head or torso, resulting in life-threatening conditions such as [intracerebral hemorrhage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intracerebral_hemorrhage "Intracerebral hemorrhage") and [peritonitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peritonitis "Peritonitis"), caused by colliding with other players, goalposts or stadium architecture. Challenging another player by targeting their body, an important part of soccer for most of the 20th century, is penalised automatically under modern refereeing guidelines, as is "dangerous play" such as playing the ball with a foot above shoulder height.

As with other forms of outdoor recreation, fatal [lightning strikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightning_injury "Lightning injury") are a rare but persistent problem, especially at training grounds where there is no stadium structure to draw the lightning away.

## List

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_association_footballers_who_died_after_on-field_incidents&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: List")]

The list includes players who died either during matches or training, or as the result of incidents during matches or training for various reasons, such as injuries, cardiac arrest, natural death, and sometimes for unknown reasons. Death may occur immediately or several days after the injury or fall, but is still directly attributable to football-related activities.

It does not include players who suffered cardiac "death" on the pitch but were successfully resuscitated and survived, such as [Fabrice Muamba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabrice_Muamba "Fabrice Muamba") and [Christian Eriksen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Eriksen "Christian Eriksen").

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
This is a dynamic list and may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness. You can help by editing the page to add missing items, with references to reliable sources.

This is a list of association footballers who died due to football-related incidents.

The primary causes of on-field deaths have evolved over time. Improvements in infection control and emergency surgery since the early days of organised soccer have mostly eliminated the fatal complications that were once common after routine sporting injuries. Squad rotation and substitutes have also reduced the need for seriously ill players to start, or remain in, games, and lifestyle factors are now tightly controlled.

However, deaths from heart failure have increased as the intense pace of the modern game has placed higher demands on players' aerobic conditioning. Following an increase in heart-related deaths,[1] both during matches and training, in 2007 the International Federation of Association Football (FIFA) considered mandatory cardiac testing,[2] already in place for years in some countries, such as Italy.[3] By 2009, FIFA pre-competition medical assessment included family history, heart rhythm, sounds, and electrocardiogram results.[4] The Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) required extensive medical tests, including electrocardiogram and echocardiogram for players in the Europa League 2011–12.[5] Constant monitoring has been advised.[6]

The FIFA Sudden Death Report (FIFA-SDR) was carried out by Saarland University and published in 2020.[7] The report recorded worldwide deaths attributed to sudden cardiac arrest or other unexplained sudden death while playing (or shortly after playing) football from 2014 to 2018. There were 617 cases during the five-year period. In the majority of cases where an autopsy was carried out, the cause of death was coronary heart disease.

Most non-cardiac deaths are the result of blunt trauma to the head or torso, resulting in life-threatening conditions such as intracerebral hemorrhage and peritonitis, caused by colliding with other players, goalposts or stadium architecture. Challenging another player by targeting their body, an important part of soccer for most of the 20th century, is penalised automatically under modern refereeing guidelines, as is "dangerous play" such as playing the ball with a foot above shoulder height.

As with other forms of outdoor recreation, fatal lightning strikes are a rare but persistent problem, especially at training grounds where there is no stadium structure to draw the lightning away.

Listedit

The list includes players who died either during matches or training, or as the result of incidents during matches or training for various reasons, such as injuries, cardiac arrest, natural death, and sometimes for unknown reasons. Death may occur immediately or several days after the injury or fall, but is still directly attributable to football-related activities.

It does not include players who suffered cardiac "death" on the pitch but were successfully resuscitated and survived, such as Fabrice Muamba and Christian Eriksen.

**Original Question:**

The last scorer in the game was instrumental in this player's first-half scoring. This rivalry game is a well-known event in the country. From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
This is a dynamic list and may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness. You can help by editing the page to add missing items, with references to reliable sources.

This is a list of association footballers who died due to football-related incidents.

The primary causes of on-field deaths have evolved over time. Improvements in infection control and emergency surgery since the early days of organised soccer have mostly eliminated the fatal complications that were once common after routine sporting injuries. Squad rotation and substitutes have also reduced the need for seriously ill players to start, or remain in, games, and lifestyle factors are now tightly controlled.

However, deaths from heart failure have increased as the intense pace of the modern game has placed higher demands on players' aerobic conditioning. Following an increase in heart-related deaths,[1] both during matches and training, in 2007 the International Federation of Association Football (FIFA) considered mandatory cardiac testing,[2] already in place for years in some countries, such as Italy.[3] By 2009, FIFA pre-competition medical assessment included family history, heart rhythm, sounds, and electrocardiogram results.[4] The Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) required extensive medical tests, including electrocardiogram and echocardiogram for players in the Europa League 2011–12.[5] Constant monitoring has been advised.[6]

The FIFA Sudden Death Report (FIFA-SDR) was carried out by Saarland University and published in 2020.[7] The report recorded worldwide deaths attributed to sudden cardiac arrest or other unexplained sudden death while playing (or shortly after playing) football from 2014 to 2018. There were 617 cases during the five-year period. In the majority of cases where an autopsy was carried out, the cause of death was coronary heart disease.

Most non-cardiac deaths are the result of blunt trauma to the head or torso, resulting in life-threatening conditions such as intracerebral hemorrhage and peritonitis, caused by colliding with other players, goalposts or stadium architecture. Challenging another player by targeting their body, an important part of soccer for most of the 20th century, is penalised automatically under modern refereeing guidelines, as is "dangerous play" such as playing the ball with a foot above shoulder height.

As with other forms of outdoor recreation, fatal lightning strikes are a rare but persistent problem, especially at training grounds where there is no stadium structure to draw the lightning away.

Listedit

The list includes players who died either during matches or training, or as the result of incidents during matches or training for various reasons, such as injuries, cardiac arrest, natural death, and sometimes for unknown reasons. Death may occur immediately or several days after the injury or fall, but is still directly attributable to football-related activities.

It does not include players who suffered cardiac "death" on the pitch but were successfully resuscitated and survived, such as Fabrice Muamba and Christian Eriksen.

**Cristiano Sebastião de Lima Júnior** (5 June 1979 – 5 December 2004) was a Brazilian [footballer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") who played as a [forward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_(association_football) "Forward (association football)") for [Dempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dempo_S.C. "Dempo S.C."),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior#cite_note-1) before an on-field collision in India in the [Federation Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_Cup_(India) "Federation Cup (India)") finals, with the goalkeeper of the opposing team led to his death.

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

Júnior, who was the highest-paid footballer in [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"), signed up for Dempo in September 2004. He had only recently moved to Dempo on a transfer from Kolkata's [East Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Bengal_F.C. "East Bengal F.C.") where he had formed a potent strike partnership with India's footballer [Baichung Bhutia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baichung_Bhutia "Baichung Bhutia") in helping his team win the league title in the 2003-2004 season and reach the knock-out stages of the [2004 AFC Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_AFC_Cup "2004 AFC Cup").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Death")]

Júnior collided with [Mohun Bagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohun_Bagan "Mohun Bagan") goalkeeper [Subrata Pal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subrata_Pal "Subrata Pal"), in the 78th minute of the [Federation Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_Cup_(India) "Federation Cup (India)") finals. While scoring his second goal after chasing the ball into the box, he collided with the keeper, staggered away and then collapsed.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior#cite_note-2) Attempts to revive him were unsuccessful. The game continued after Junior was taken off the field. He was [dead on arrival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_on_arrival "Dead on arrival") at [Hosmat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hosmat "Hosmat") Hospital. Hospital officials said that no doctors were requested to be at the ground during the Federation Cup match. "At no time, was the hospital requested to provide doctors, and no agreement or contract for doctors was made."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior#cite_note-3) Dempo won the Cup 2-0. According to the autopsy performed in the Bangalore Hospital (where Junior was moved from the stadium), the footballer died because of a [heart stroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_stroke "Heart stroke"). The report also added that Júnior was not injured at the moment of the arrival to the health center.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior#cite_note-4)

Dempo announced that they would retire Júnior's #10 shirt.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior#cite_note-5) It filed a complaint of criminal negligence against Subrata Pal, Hosmat Hospital, and the [Karnataka State Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karnataka_State_Football_Association "Karnataka State Football Association"), the local organizers. Pal was suspended for 2 months.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior#cite_note-6)

**Cristiano Sebastião de Lima Júnior** (5 June 1979 – 5 December 2004) was a Brazilian [footballer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") who played as a [forward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_(association_football) "Forward (association football)") for [Dempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dempo_S.C. "Dempo S.C."),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior#cite_note-1) before an on-field collision in India in the [Federation Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_Cup_(India) "Federation Cup (India)") finals, with the goalkeeper of the opposing team led to his death.

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

Júnior, who was the highest-paid footballer in [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"), signed up for Dempo in September 2004. He had only recently moved to Dempo on a transfer from Kolkata's [East Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Bengal_F.C. "East Bengal F.C.") where he had formed a potent strike partnership with India's footballer [Baichung Bhutia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baichung_Bhutia "Baichung Bhutia") in helping his team win the league title in the 2003-2004 season and reach the knock-out stages of the [2004 AFC Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_AFC_Cup "2004 AFC Cup").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Death")]

Júnior collided with [Mohun Bagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohun_Bagan "Mohun Bagan") goalkeeper [Subrata Pal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subrata_Pal "Subrata Pal"), in the 78th minute of the [Federation Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_Cup_(India) "Federation Cup (India)") finals. While scoring his second goal after chasing the ball into the box, he collided with the keeper, staggered away and then collapsed.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior#cite_note-2) Attempts to revive him were unsuccessful. The game continued after Junior was taken off the field. He was [dead on arrival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_on_arrival "Dead on arrival") at [Hosmat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hosmat "Hosmat") Hospital. Hospital officials said that no doctors were requested to be at the ground during the Federation Cup match. "At no time, was the hospital requested to provide doctors, and no agreement or contract for doctors was made."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior#cite_note-3) Dempo won the Cup 2-0. According to the autopsy performed in the Bangalore Hospital (where Junior was moved from the stadium), the footballer died because of a [heart stroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_stroke "Heart stroke"). The report also added that Júnior was not injured at the moment of the arrival to the health center.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior#cite_note-4)

Dempo announced that they would retire Júnior's #10 shirt.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior#cite_note-5) It filed a complaint of criminal negligence against Subrata Pal, Hosmat Hospital, and the [Karnataka State Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karnataka_State_Football_Association "Karnataka State Football Association"), the local organizers. Pal was suspended for 2 months.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_J%C3%BAnior#cite_note-6)

**Antonio José Puerta Pérez** (Spanish pronunciation:[[anˈtonjo ˈpweɾta]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish"); 26 November 1984 – 28 August 2007) was a Spanish professional [footballer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") who played solely for [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-1)

Mainly a [left midfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midfielder#Wide_midfielder "Midfielder") who could also operate as an attacking [left-back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defender_(association_football)#Full-back "Defender (association football)"), he died on 28 August 2007 affected with [arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrhythmogenic_cardiomyopathy "Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy"), three days after suffering a series of [cardiac arrests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_arrest "Cardiac arrest") during a [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") game against [Getafe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getafe_CF "Getafe CF") on the 25th.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-2)

Puerta won five trophies with his only club, and appeared once for [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_national_football_team "Spain national football team").

## Club career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antonio_Puerta&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Club career")]

Born in [Seville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seville "Seville"), [Andalusia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andalusia "Andalusia"), Puerta joined [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC") as a boy and spent a total of 14 years at the club,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-Guardian-3) growing up at its acclaimed youth system alongside other players such as [Alejandro Alfaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alejandro_Alfaro "Alejandro Alfaro"), [Kepa Blanco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kepa_Blanco "Kepa Blanco"), [Jesús Navas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jes%C3%BAs_Navas "Jesús Navas"), [Sergio Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ramos "Sergio Ramos") and [José Antonio Reyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Antonio_Reyes "José Antonio Reyes"). His [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") debut came on 21 March 2004, as he played 71 minutes in a 0–1 home defeat against neighbours [Málaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A1laga_CF "Málaga CF").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-4)

Promoted to the first team for the [2005–06 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_La_Liga "2005–06 La Liga"), Puerta became intimately connected to Sevilla's history on 27 April 2006, when he scored against [Schalke 04](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Schalke_04 "FC Schalke 04") in [the semi-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_UEFA_Cup "2005–06 UEFA Cup") of the [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League"): in the final moments of the match, he received a long ball and struck it with his left foot for the 1–0 final (and aggregate) win;[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-5) they went on to collect five titles in fifteen months, with Puerta scoring his [penalty shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") attempt in the [2007 UEFA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_UEFA_Cup_final "2007 UEFA Cup final"), against compatriots [Espanyol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCD_Espanyol "RCD Espanyol").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-6) His impressive performances earned him international recognition and reported interest from [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C."), [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") and [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-7) but all bids were rejected.

### Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antonio_Puerta&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Death")]

On 25 August 2007, Puerta collapsed and lost consciousness in the [penalty area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_area "Penalty area") due to a cardiac arrest during Sevilla's first [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") fixture of the [2007–08 campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_La_Liga "2007–08 La Liga") at the [Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_S%C3%A1nchez-Pizju%C3%A1n_Stadium "Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium") against [Getafe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getafe_CF "Getafe CF").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-8) He was seen crouching and then subsequently collapsing upon moving back to his team's [goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_(sports) "Goal (sports)") after only 35 minutes of the game had passed,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-Guardian-3) as teammates [Ivica Dragutinović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivica_Dragutinovi%C4%87 "Ivica Dragutinović") and [Andrés Palop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_Palop "Andrés Palop") immediately ran to his side as he lost consciousness; moments later, club medical staff and other players followed suit.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-9)

After recovering and being substituted, Puerta was able to walk to the dressing room, where he collapsed once again. He was resuscitated by the doctors and taken, by ambulance, to the [intensive care unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intensive_care_unit "Intensive care unit") of _Virgen del Rocío_ hospital, where he received [cardiopulmonary resuscitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiopulmonary_resuscitation "Cardiopulmonary resuscitation").

Puerta died on 28 August 2007, at 14:30.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-11) Doctor Francisco Murillo reported that he had suffered [multiple organ failure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple_organ_dysfunction_syndrome "Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome") and irreversible [brain damage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain_damage "Brain damage") as a result of multiple prolonged cardiac arrests due to an incurable, [hereditary heart disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congenital_Heart_Disease "Congenital Heart Disease") known as [arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrhythmogenic_cardiomyopathy "Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-12)

Puerta's girlfriend was expecting their first child at the time of his death.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-Guardian-3) As a mark of respect, players from both Sevilla and city rivals [Real Betis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis "Real Betis") attended his funeral days after his death and, subsequently, [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA") ordered the installation of resuscitation rooms in every stadium that hosted the [World Cup qualifiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_qualification "FIFA World Cup qualification").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-13)

### Tributes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antonio_Puerta&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Tributes")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/Camisetapuerta.JPG/250px-Camisetapuerta.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Camisetapuerta.JPG)

Sevilla retired Puerta's number 16 jersey after his death

As a result of Puerta's death, Sevilla's [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League")[qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_UEFA_Champions_League "2007–08 UEFA Champions League") against [AEK Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AEK_Athens_F.C. "AEK Athens F.C.") was postponed until 3 September;[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-14) the former eventually won 4–1.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-15) It was also announced that a [one-minute silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moment_of_silence "Moment of silence") would be held before every Spanish league match that weekend.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-16)

Additionally, the team's [UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Super_Cup "UEFA Super Cup")[game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_UEFA_Super_Cup "2007 UEFA Super Cup") with [AC Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") on 31 August went ahead, as a tribute to Puerta, with all 22 participants having the name 'PUERTA' printed on the back of their jersey. The players and officials on both sides also wore black armbands.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-17)

Sevilla subsequently [retired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_retired_numbers_in_association_football "List of retired numbers in association football") Puerta's number 16 shirt, with the provision that should his son, Aitor Antonio (born 22 October 2007),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-18) one day play for the club, he would have the option to bring the number out of retirement.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-19) However, Spanish football teams were not allowed to do so, as the [Royal Spanish Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Spanish_Football_Federation "Royal Spanish Football Federation") stated that clubs should use number 1 to 25 for their regular squad, with no additional room for manoeuvre; as a result, [David Prieto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Prieto "David Prieto") wore the shirt in 2007–08 in honour of his friend[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-20) but it was later decided that only youth products could wear that jersey.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-21)

Controversially, the number was given to Argentine [Federico Fazio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Fazio "Federico Fazio") in 2016.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-22) One year later, it was awarded to [Jesús Navas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jes%C3%BAs_Navas "Jesús Navas"), a close friend of Puerta, upon his return in 2017.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-23)

Ramos wore T-shirts in memory of Puerta after Spain won [UEFA Euro 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008 "UEFA Euro 2008") and the [2010 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup "2010 FIFA World Cup"), with Navas doing the same on the latter occasion.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-24) Earlier in 2010, a statue of him was built in the club's José Ramón Cisneros Palacios sporting facilities.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-26)

## International career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antonio_Puerta&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: International career")]

Puerta was [capped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cap_(sport) "Cap (sport)") once by the [Spain national side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_national_football_team "Spain national football team"), playing against [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden_men's_national_football_team "Sweden men's national football team") on 7 October 2006. He came on as a [substitute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)") for [Deportivo de La Coruña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deportivo_de_La_Coru%C3%B1a "Deportivo de La Coruña")'s [Joan Capdevila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Capdevila "Joan Capdevila") in the 52nd minute of a 2–0 away loss for the [UEFA Euro 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008 "UEFA Euro 2008")[qualifiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008_qualifying "UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-27)

Additionally, Puerta appeared five times for [the under-21s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_national_under-21_football_team "Spain national under-21 football team").

**Antonio José Puerta Pérez** (Spanish pronunciation:[[anˈtonjo ˈpweɾta]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish"); 26 November 1984 – 28 August 2007) was a Spanish professional [footballer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") who played solely for [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-1)

Mainly a [left midfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midfielder#Wide_midfielder "Midfielder") who could also operate as an attacking [left-back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defender_(association_football)#Full-back "Defender (association football)"), he died on 28 August 2007 affected with [arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrhythmogenic_cardiomyopathy "Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy"), three days after suffering a series of [cardiac arrests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_arrest "Cardiac arrest") during a [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") game against [Getafe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getafe_CF "Getafe CF") on the 25th.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-2)

Puerta won five trophies with his only club, and appeared once for [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_national_football_team "Spain national football team").

## Club career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antonio_Puerta&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Club career")]

Born in [Seville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seville "Seville"), [Andalusia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andalusia "Andalusia"), Puerta joined [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC") as a boy and spent a total of 14 years at the club,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-Guardian-3) growing up at its acclaimed youth system alongside other players such as [Alejandro Alfaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alejandro_Alfaro "Alejandro Alfaro"), [Kepa Blanco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kepa_Blanco "Kepa Blanco"), [Jesús Navas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jes%C3%BAs_Navas "Jesús Navas"), [Sergio Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ramos "Sergio Ramos") and [José Antonio Reyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Antonio_Reyes "José Antonio Reyes"). His [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") debut came on 21 March 2004, as he played 71 minutes in a 0–1 home defeat against neighbours [Málaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A1laga_CF "Málaga CF").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-4)

Promoted to the first team for the [2005–06 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_La_Liga "2005–06 La Liga"), Puerta became intimately connected to Sevilla's history on 27 April 2006, when he scored against [Schalke 04](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Schalke_04 "FC Schalke 04") in [the semi-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_UEFA_Cup "2005–06 UEFA Cup") of the [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League"): in the final moments of the match, he received a long ball and struck it with his left foot for the 1–0 final (and aggregate) win;[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-5) they went on to collect five titles in fifteen months, with Puerta scoring his [penalty shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") attempt in the [2007 UEFA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_UEFA_Cup_final "2007 UEFA Cup final"), against compatriots [Espanyol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCD_Espanyol "RCD Espanyol").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-6) His impressive performances earned him international recognition and reported interest from [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C."), [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") and [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-7) but all bids were rejected.

### Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antonio_Puerta&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Death")]

On 25 August 2007, Puerta collapsed and lost consciousness in the [penalty area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_area "Penalty area") due to a cardiac arrest during Sevilla's first [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") fixture of the [2007–08 campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_La_Liga "2007–08 La Liga") at the [Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_S%C3%A1nchez-Pizju%C3%A1n_Stadium "Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium") against [Getafe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getafe_CF "Getafe CF").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-8) He was seen crouching and then subsequently collapsing upon moving back to his team's [goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_(sports) "Goal (sports)") after only 35 minutes of the game had passed,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-Guardian-3) as teammates [Ivica Dragutinović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivica_Dragutinovi%C4%87 "Ivica Dragutinović") and [Andrés Palop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_Palop "Andrés Palop") immediately ran to his side as he lost consciousness; moments later, club medical staff and other players followed suit.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-9)

After recovering and being substituted, Puerta was able to walk to the dressing room, where he collapsed once again. He was resuscitated by the doctors and taken, by ambulance, to the [intensive care unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intensive_care_unit "Intensive care unit") of _Virgen del Rocío_ hospital, where he received [cardiopulmonary resuscitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiopulmonary_resuscitation "Cardiopulmonary resuscitation").

Puerta died on 28 August 2007, at 14:30.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-11) Doctor Francisco Murillo reported that he had suffered [multiple organ failure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple_organ_dysfunction_syndrome "Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome") and irreversible [brain damage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain_damage "Brain damage") as a result of multiple prolonged cardiac arrests due to an incurable, [hereditary heart disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congenital_Heart_Disease "Congenital Heart Disease") known as [arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrhythmogenic_cardiomyopathy "Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-12)

Puerta's girlfriend was expecting their first child at the time of his death.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-Guardian-3) As a mark of respect, players from both Sevilla and city rivals [Real Betis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis "Real Betis") attended his funeral days after his death and, subsequently, [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA") ordered the installation of resuscitation rooms in every stadium that hosted the [World Cup qualifiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_qualification "FIFA World Cup qualification").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-13)

### Tributes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antonio_Puerta&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Tributes")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/Camisetapuerta.JPG/250px-Camisetapuerta.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Camisetapuerta.JPG)

Sevilla retired Puerta's number 16 jersey after his death

As a result of Puerta's death, Sevilla's [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League")[qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_UEFA_Champions_League "2007–08 UEFA Champions League") against [AEK Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AEK_Athens_F.C. "AEK Athens F.C.") was postponed until 3 September;[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-14) the former eventually won 4–1.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-15) It was also announced that a [one-minute silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moment_of_silence "Moment of silence") would be held before every Spanish league match that weekend.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-16)

Additionally, the team's [UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Super_Cup "UEFA Super Cup")[game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_UEFA_Super_Cup "2007 UEFA Super Cup") with [AC Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") on 31 August went ahead, as a tribute to Puerta, with all 22 participants having the name 'PUERTA' printed on the back of their jersey. The players and officials on both sides also wore black armbands.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-17)

Sevilla subsequently [retired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_retired_numbers_in_association_football "List of retired numbers in association football") Puerta's number 16 shirt, with the provision that should his son, Aitor Antonio (born 22 October 2007),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-18) one day play for the club, he would have the option to bring the number out of retirement.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-19) However, Spanish football teams were not allowed to do so, as the [Royal Spanish Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Spanish_Football_Federation "Royal Spanish Football Federation") stated that clubs should use number 1 to 25 for their regular squad, with no additional room for manoeuvre; as a result, [David Prieto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Prieto "David Prieto") wore the shirt in 2007–08 in honour of his friend[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-20) but it was later decided that only youth products could wear that jersey.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-21)

Controversially, the number was given to Argentine [Federico Fazio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Fazio "Federico Fazio") in 2016.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-22) One year later, it was awarded to [Jesús Navas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jes%C3%BAs_Navas "Jesús Navas"), a close friend of Puerta, upon his return in 2017.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-23)

Ramos wore T-shirts in memory of Puerta after Spain won [UEFA Euro 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008 "UEFA Euro 2008") and the [2010 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup "2010 FIFA World Cup"), with Navas doing the same on the latter occasion.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-24) Earlier in 2010, a statue of him was built in the club's José Ramón Cisneros Palacios sporting facilities.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-26)

## International career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antonio_Puerta&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: International career")]

Puerta was [capped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cap_(sport) "Cap (sport)") once by the [Spain national side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_national_football_team "Spain national football team"), playing against [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden_men's_national_football_team "Sweden men's national football team") on 7 October 2006. He came on as a [substitute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)") for [Deportivo de La Coruña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deportivo_de_La_Coru%C3%B1a "Deportivo de La Coruña")'s [Joan Capdevila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Capdevila "Joan Capdevila") in the 52nd minute of a 2–0 away loss for the [UEFA Euro 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008 "UEFA Euro 2008")[qualifiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008_qualifying "UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Puerta#cite_note-27)

Additionally, Puerta appeared five times for [the under-21s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_national_under-21_football_team "Spain national under-21 football team").

**Sevilla Fútbol Club** (Spanish pronunciation:[[seˈβiʎa ˈfuðβol ˈkluβ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish")) is a Spanish professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in [Seville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seville "Seville"), [Andalusia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andalusia "Andalusia"), that competes in [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga"), the [top flight of Spanish football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_football_league_system "Spanish football league system"). The club was formed on 25 January 1890, making it Spain's second oldest sporting club solely devoted to football, after [Recreativo de Huelva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recreativo_de_Huelva "Recreativo de Huelva").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-Marca-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-Evening_Times-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-8) The Scottish-born [Edward Farquharson Johnston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_F._Johnston "Edward F. Johnston") was one of Sevilla's founders, also becoming their first president. On 14 October 1905, the club's articles of association were registered in the Civil Government of Seville under the presidency of the Jerez-born José Luis Gallegos Arnosa.

Sevilla are also the most successful football club in [Andalusia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andalusia "Andalusia") in terms of titles, with eighteen Andalusian Cups,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-9) one [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") title in [1945–46](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1945%E2%80%9346_La_Liga "1945–46 La Liga"), five [Spanish Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey "Copa del Rey") titles ([1935](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1935_Copa_del_Presidente_de_la_Rep%C3%BAblica "1935 Copa del Presidente de la República"), [1939](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1939_Copa_del_General%C3%ADsimo "1939 Copa del Generalísimo"),
