They were also designated by the [International Federation of Football History & Statistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_Football_History_&_Statistics "International Federation of Football History & Statistics") as the [World's Best Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFFHS_World's_Best_Club "IFFHS World's Best Club") in 2006 and 2007, thus being the first club to achieve this distinction in two consecutive years.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-:0-10)

The reserve team [Sevilla Atlético](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_Atl%C3%A9tico "Sevilla Atlético"), founded in 1958, currently play in [Segunda Federación](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Segunda_Federaci%C3%B3n "Segunda Federación") – Group 4. Other clubs related to Sevilla FC include their women's team. The rowing team that defends its crest in the yearly Sevilla-Betis [boat race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boat_racing "Boat racing") is not a section of the club but a call-up of registered-as-supporters professional rowers from the various rowing clubs of Seville.

The club's home ground is the 43,883-seat [Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_S%C3%A1nchez-Pizju%C3%A1n_Stadium "Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium"). It is located in the neighborhood of [Nervión, Seville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervi%C3%B3n,_Seville "Nervión, Seville"), and is named after [Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_S%C3%A1nchez-Pizju%C3%A1n "Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán"), who was the president of Sevilla for 17 years. Sevilla has a long-standing rivalry with cross-city rival [Real Betis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis "Real Betis"), and matches between the pair are the [Seville derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seville_derby "Seville derby").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sevilla_FC&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Foundation to Civil War

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sevilla_FC&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Foundation to Civil War")]

The practice of football was introduced in Seville at the end of the 19th century by the large British expatriate population in the city, composed by owners or managers of manufacturing companies based in the capital of [Andalusia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andalusia "Andalusia"). **Sevilla Fútbol Club** was founded on [Burns Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burns_Night "Burns Night") 25 January 1890 as _Sevilla Foot-ball Club_ (in English).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-The_British_Newspaper_Archive-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-The_Courier-12)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-Marca-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-Evening_Times-7)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-Historia-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-Historia4-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-16)[_[excessive citations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing\_sources#Bundling\_citations "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_]

Sevilla FC was duly formed on 25 January 1890 while a group of young British, mainly Scots, along with other young men of Spanish origin, celebrated [Burns Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burns_supper "Burns supper") in Seville.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-17) The club's founding document, published on the _[Dundee Courier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dundee\_Courier "Dundee Courier")'_ s edition of 17 March 1890 describes in full detail the formation of the club and how those young founding members decided first to play under Association Rules, secondly to bear the word "football" within its name and thirdly, to elect their "office-bearers". The following paragraph is an extract of that article:

> Some six weeks ago a few enthusiastic young residents of British origin met in one of the cafés for the purpose of considering a proposal that we should start an Athletic Association, the want of exercise being greatly felt by the majority of us, who are chiefly engaged in mercantile pursuits. After a deal of talk and limited consumption of small beer, the "Club de Football de Sevilla" was duly formed and office-bearers elected. It was decided we should play Association rules (...) We were about half and half Spanish and British

[![Image 43](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/72/Edward_Farquharson_Johnston.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Edward_Farquharson_Johnston.png)

[Edward F. Johnston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_F._Johnston "Edward F. Johnston"), founder, and the first President

The club's first president was the Scot Mr. [Edward Farquharson Johnston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_F._Johnston "Edward F. Johnston") (Elgin, 14 October 1854), who was the British vice-consul in Seville and co-proprietor of the firm MacAndrews & Co., ship-owners with commercial lines between Spain and the UK, one of them being the transport of [Seville oranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seville_orange "Seville orange"). [Hugh MacColl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_MacColl_(footballer) "Hugh MacColl (footballer)"), another Scottish young man (Glasgow, 9 June 1861), a marine engineer who at that time had moved to Seville to work as the technical manager of Portilla White foundry, was their first captain. One of Maccoll's partners in the Portilla White foundry in Seville, Isaias White junior, was the club's first secretary. He was the son of an English entrepreneur who founded the aforesaid company, one of the major foundries in Spain at the end of the 19th century.

To celebrate the foundation of the club, [Isaias White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaias_White "Isaias White") sent a letter to Huelva Recreation Club, to invite them to play a football match in Seville. That letter was published by the Spanish newspaper _La Provincia_. The Huelva club accepted the invitation and the match took place on 8 March 1890, being thus the [first official match ever played in Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_football_match_in_Spain "First football match in Spain").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-18) Sevilla FC won that historical match 2–0, with the first goal in an official match in Spanish football history scored by the Seville team player Ritson. Isaias lived at Calle Bailen 41[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-19) in Seville (the house still exists but has since been renumbered) making this the first home of Sevilla FC.

In 1907, Sevilla Balompíe was founded, followed by Betis Football Club in 1909, Recreativo de Sevilla and Español de Sevilla. More clubs were formed as the years passed and more competitive matches were organized between the teams, although Sevilla FC, the oldest club of the city, imposed its supremacy over the other clubs in this early period.

[![Image 44](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Sevilla_F%C3%BAtbol_Club_-_Real_Club_Recreativo_de_Huelva_%281909%29.jpg/330px-Sevilla_F%C3%BAtbol_Club_-_Real_Club_Recreativo_de_Huelva_%281909%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sevilla_F%C3%BAtbol_Club_-_Real_Club_Recreativo_de_Huelva_(1909).jpg)

Sevilla Fútbol Club – Real Club Recreativo de Huelva (1909)

In 1912, the first Copa de Sevilla was played and won by Sevilla FC. From 1915 to 1940, the [Campeonato Regional Sur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campeonato_Regional_Sur "Campeonato Regional Sur") (also known as the Copa Andalucía) was organized by the "Federación Sur" ([Andalusian FA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Andalusian_Football_Federation "Royal Andalusian Football Federation")) and these championships included Sevilla FC, Real Betis Balompié, Recreativo de Huelva, Español de Cádiz and the sporadic participation of other clubs such as Nacional de Sevilla and Córdoba. The domination of Sevilla was so evident that of the 20 championships played, 17 were won by Sevilla FC, (the three remaining being won by Español de de Cádiz, Recreativo de Huelva and Real Betis Balompié).

In 1917, Sevilla FC participated in the "Copa de España" for the first time and became the first Andalusian team to reach the final round of the competition. In 1928, when the "Campeonato Nacional de Liga" (National League Championships) was organized, Sevilla FC was not part of the First Division due to their defeat to [Racing de Santander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racing_de_Santander "Racing de Santander") in an elimination game that was set up to decide which of the two teams would compete in the newly formed league.

At the end of the 1933–34 season, Sevilla FC was promoted to the First Division of the "Campeonato Nacional de Liga." In 1935, they were proclaimed "Campeón de Copa" (Cup Champions) for the first time by defeating [Sabadell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CE_Sabadell_FC "CE Sabadell FC"), repeated in 1939 against [Racing de Ferrol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racing_de_Ferrol "Racing de Ferrol") and again in 1948 against [Celta de Vigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celta_de_Vigo "Celta de Vigo"). The club participated in two other finals, but conceded defeat to [Athletic Bilbao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletic_Bilbao "Athletic Bilbao") in 1955 and to [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_C.F. "Real Madrid C.F.") in 1962. Sevilla FC remained in the First Division from the 1933–34 season until 1968, when they were relegated to the Second Division, a tier from which they have never further been relegated from.

[![Image 45](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/Priemrescudodelsevilla2.JPG/250px-Priemrescudodelsevilla2.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Priemrescudodelsevilla2.JPG)

Sevilla's first crest, displayed on a former player's shirt in the club museum

The 1945–46 season was one of high importance in the history of Sevilla, as it marked the first, and to date only, time in which Sevilla FC were League champions. On four other occasions, the club was proclaimed "subcampeón de Liga" (League Runner-up: 1939–40, 1942–43, 1950–51 and 1956–57).

Including the 2021–22 season, Sevilla has participated 78 times in the First Division and 13 in the Second Division, never dropping below the Second Division. Sevilla has also participated in four European tournaments, the "Copa de Europa" (European League Winners Cup) (1957–58); Recopa (Winners Cup) (1962–63) and [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League") on nine occasions (1966–67, 1970–71, 1982–83, 1983–84, 1990–91, 1995–96, 2004–05, 2005–06 and 2006–07). Sevilla also participated in the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") in [2007–08](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_UEFA_Champions_League "2007–08 UEFA Champions League").

There are more than 400 individuals who currently play for the Sevilla FC organization, which includes two semi-professional teams (in Second Division A – second national category) and 12 youth teams.

[![Image 46](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Balondefutbol1924.JPG/250px-Balondefutbol1924.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Balondefutbol1924.JPG)

Club ball in the museum

Sevilla has always counted on having international players within its ranks to aid in the pursuit of trophies. The first of these players were Spencer and Herminio in the 1920s. Juan Arza, an international player from the 1940s, was proclaimed top scorer of the Spanish League in the 1954–55 season, with 29 goals. About 30 Sevilla players have been chosen to play for the [Spain national football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_men's_national_football_team "Spain men's national football team") over the years.

Foreign players have always played an integral part in the success of Sevilla FC with Diego Maradona representing the most well known among them during his spell with the club during the 1992–93 season. During the same season, Sevilla FC was managed by Carlos Salvador Bilardo, a world champion manager.

Historically, Sevilla FC has fielded teams in a variety of other sports including: basketball, rugby, rowing, athletics, and [weightlifting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_weightlifting "Olympic weightlifting") or petanca. Presently, Sevilla FC counts twenty-five professional teams on its ledgers (one of these being in the second national category) and a women's football team in the Honor Division.

Sevilla FC's stadium, the [Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_S%C3%A1nchez_Pizju%C3%A1n_Stadium "Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium"), was inaugurated in 1958 and is one of the largest stadiums in Spain, and has the honor of hosting a World Cup semi-final match in [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup "1982 FIFA World Cup"). After its final completion, the stadium had a maximum capacity of 75,000 spectators, but since its latest remodelling, the stadium has been converted to an all-seat with a covering added to the main seating area, reducing the capacity to its current count of 45,000 spectators.

### First successes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sevilla_FC&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: First successes")]

[![Image 47](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Suscripcionpopularnuevoestadio.JPG/250px-Suscripcionpopularnuevoestadio.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Suscripcionpopularnuevoestadio.JPG)

Bond issue to build the new stadium (1957)

[![Image 48](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Bustoderamonsanchezpizjuan2.JPG/250px-Bustoderamonsanchezpizjuan2.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bustoderamonsanchezpizjuan2.JPG)

Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán's bust placed at the stadium

Sevilla had their first spell of national success in the decade following the end of the Civil War, winning the [1945–46 La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1945%E2%80%9346_La_Liga "1945–46 La Liga") title and two [Copa del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey "Copa del Rey") titles. In the first season of this (1939–40), Sevilla won the cup on 25 June, beating Racing de Ferrol 6–2 in [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-rsssf.com-20) That same season, the side lost the Liga title on the last day to [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") after drawing 3–3 against [Hércules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9rcules_CF "Hércules CF").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-21) The Sevilla forward line was known as _los stukas_ after the [German bomber aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junkers_Ju_87 "Junkers Ju 87"), and scored 216 goals over four seasons. It comprised López, Torrontegui, [Campanal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campanal_I "Campanal I"), Raimundo, Berrocal and [Pepillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepillo_(footballer,_born_1916) "Pepillo (footballer, born 1916)").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-Historia4-15)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-22)

In 1941, President [Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_S%C3%A1nchez_Pizju%C3%A1n "Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán") left the club to manage the [Spanish Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Spanish_Football_Federation "Royal Spanish Football Federation"). After his departure, Antonio Sánchez Ramos occupied temporarily occupied the position until the permanent appointment of [Jerónimo Domínguez y Pérez de Vargas, Marquess of Contadero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jer%C3%B3nimo_P%C3%A9rez_de_Vargas?action=edit&redlink=1 "Jerónimo Pérez de Vargas (page does not exist)"), who was president of the club for six years until the return of Sánchez Pizjuán.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-23) Sevilla was runner-up to Athletic Bilbao in the 1942–43 season and came third a season later. Sevilla won its only Liga title in 1945–46, edging [FC Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") by one point.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-24) Two years later, Sevilla won the [1948 Copa del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Copa_del_Rey "1948 Copa del Rey") after beating Celta de Vigo 4–1 in [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") on 4 July.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-rsssf.com-20)

The most significant signing of those years was the Spanish international striker [Juan Arza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Arza "Juan Arza"). There was also the debut of the Campanal's nephew, defender Campanal II, with his uncle as a trainer. During the 1950–51 season, with Campanal acting as the coach, the team finished runner-up in La Liga, two points behind Atlético Madrid.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-ReferenceA-25) Before the 1953–54 season, Argentinean coach [Helenio Herrera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helenio_Herrera "Helenio Herrera") was hired. During his time in charge, the club came fifth in the 1953–54 season, fourth in both 1954–55 and 1955–56 and second to Real Madrid in 1956–57.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-ReferenceA-25)

In 1954, the club put the construction of the new stadium out to tender because Nervión Stadium was becoming too small for the club's fanbase. In the 1954–55 season, Arza won the [Pichichi Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pichichi_Trophy "Pichichi Trophy") as La Liga's top scorer, with 28 goals,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-26) and the team was runner-up in the Copa del Rey. In 1955, for the club's 50th anniversary, a triangular tournament was organized against the French club [Stade de Reims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_de_Reims "Stade de Reims") and the Swedish club [IFK Norrköping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFK_Norrk%C3%B6ping "IFK Norrköping"); Sevilla won.

On 28 October 1956, President Sánchez Pizjuán suddenly died. As an appreciation to the deceased leader under whose chairmanship Sevilla had won three Copas del Rey, the fans decided that the club's planned new stadium was to be named in his honour.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-27) In the 1956–57 season, the team were Liga runners-up behind Real Madrid, ensuring qualification for the first time to the [European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"). Herrera left the club at the end of the season.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-28) The club needed a victory on the final day of the next season to avoid relegation but reached the round of 8 of the European Cup before being knocked out by holders and eventual champions Real Madrid.

After the death of the President, [Ramón de Carranza Gómez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_de_Carranza_G%C3%B3mez?action=edit&redlink=1 "Ramón de Carranza Gómez (page does not exist)")[[ES](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n%20de%20Carranza%20G%C3%B3mez "es:Ramón de Carranza Gómez")] assumed the position for four years. It is said that he spoke these words at Sánchez Pizjuán's tomb:

_"Dear Ramón, now your friends, among who I am honored to be one, is going to give you Christian burial, and on the following day, giving your body to the ground, we will start working and your dream that the Sevilla FC has a grand stadium will become a reality. Ramón, go in peace to heaven because your wishes will be fulfilled."_

Being true to his words, Carranza made obligation bonds amounting to 50 million pesetas, and a month and a half after Sánchez Pizjuán's death, the first stone in the stadium's construction was placed. The architect was Manuel Muñoz Monasterio, co-designer of the recently built [Santiago Bernabéu Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium"), the home of Real Madrid. The [Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_S%C3%A1nchez_Pizju%C3%A1n_Stadium "Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium") was ultimately opened on 7 September 1958 as Sevilla played an inaugural friendly against fellow Andalusian club [Real Jaén](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Ja%C3%A9n "Real Jaén"). The stadium's first official match was on the opening day of the [1958–59 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958%E2%80%9359_La_Liga "1958–59 La Liga"), where Sevilla beat cross-city Real Betis 4–2.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-29)

### Crisis and stability

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sevilla_FC&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Crisis and stability")]

[![Image 49](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/En_el_S%C3%A1nchez_Pizjuan_el_15-11-1961.jpg/250px-En_el_S%C3%A1nchez_Pizjuan_el_15-11-1961.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:En_el_S%C3%A1nchez_Pizjuan_el_15-11-1961.jpg)

Campanal clearing a ball in the Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium on 15 November 1961

In the 1970s, Sevilla was forced into selling its top players to pay off debts incurred from the construction of its new stadium; [Manuel Ruiz Sosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Ruiz_Sosa "Manuel Ruiz Sosa") transferred to Atlético Madrid, [Gallego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallego_(footballer) "Gallego (footballer)") to Barcelona and Juan Batista Agüero to Real Madrid. Moreover, part of the adjacent land to the stadium was also sold to a bank. In the [1967–68 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967%E2%80%9368_La_Liga "1967–68 La Liga"), Sevilla returned to the Second Division for the first time in 31 years but was promoted back after one season. The next season, Austrian coach [Max Merkel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Merkel "Max Merkel"), nicknamed "Mr. Whip" for his usage of severe and harsh discipline techniques and training, was hired.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-30)

That season, the club finished third in the league. However, the club was relegated again at the end of the [1972–73 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972%E2%80%9373_La_Liga "1972–73 La Liga"). In 1973, Sevilla signed their first-ever black player, Gambian winger [Biri Biri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biri_Biri "Biri Biri"), from the Danish club [Boldklubben 1901](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boldklubben_1901 "Boldklubben 1901"). He remained at the club until 1978 and became a cult figure, with an [ultra group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultras "Ultras") named after him surviving to this day. In the [1974–75 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_La_Liga "1974–75 La Liga"), with the Argentine [Roque Olsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roque_Olsen "Roque Olsen") in charge, the club returned to the First Division. In the late 1970s, Sevilla signed Argentinians such as [Héctor Scotta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Scotta "Héctor Scotta") and [Daniel Bertoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bertoni "Daniel Bertoni").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-Historia3-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-32)

Directed first by Miguel Muñoz and later by Manolo Cardo, the team participated in two consecutive seasons of the UEFA Cup from 1981 to 1983. The 75th anniversary of the club was celebrated with a variety of social events and a match against the Brazilian side [Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santos_FC "Santos FC"). In 1982, the [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup "1982 FIFA World Cup") was held in Spain and Sevilla's Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán was the venue for the semi-final match between [West Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Germany_national_football_team "West Germany national football team") and [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_national_football_team "France national football team").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-33) In 1984, Eugenio Montes Cabeza finished his 11-year presidency and was replaced by the cattle businessman Gabriel Rojas, who as the vice-president had made several advancements to the club's stadium. In the [1985–86 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985%E2%80%9386_La_Liga "1985–86 La Liga"), Manolo Cardo left his management position after five years in charge, while [Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_L%C3%B3pez_Alfaro "Francisco López Alfaro") played in the [1986 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_FIFA_World_Cup "1986 FIFA World Cup") for Spain. [Vicente Cantatore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vicente_Cantatore "Vicente Cantatore") led the club to UEFA Cup qualification at the end of the [1989–90 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989%E2%80%9390_La_Liga "1989–90 La Liga"), with Austrian forward [Toni Polster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toni_Polster "Toni Polster") scoring a club-record 33 Liga goals.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-Historia4-15)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-34)

In the [1992–93 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992%E2%80%9393_La_Liga "1992–93 La Liga"), after several months of negotiations, world-renowned Argentine [Diego Maradona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Maradona "Diego Maradona") signed from [Napoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.S.C._Napoli "S.S.C. Napoli") for a fee of $7.5 million. His time at the club, however, was unsuccessful, and he was released in large part due to his periodic injuries and clashes with coach Bilardo.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-35) In the following seasons, [Luis Aragonés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Aragon%C3%A9s "Luis Aragonés") became manager and finished the [1994–95 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994%E2%80%9395_La_Liga "1994–95 La Liga") with qualification to next season's UEFA Cup.

At the end of the 1994–95 season, despite the pleas of the club's directors, Sevilla, along with Celta de Vigo, were one of two clubs relegated from the top flight on reasons of administration, provoking action from fans. The action resulted in both Sevilla and Celta being reinstated to La Liga.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-36)

These events led to an institutional instability, with the season seeing four presidents and three managers take charge. Sevilla was relegated at the end of the [1996–97 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996%E2%80%9397_La_Liga "1996–97 La Liga"), after 22 years stayed in top division, but returned in 1999.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-37) At the beginning of the 21st century, the presidency of the club was assumed by the popular Roberto Alés.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-38) The situation of the club was very delicate at the time; the team had dropped back to the Second Division in 2000 and the squad was weakened by player retirements and the sales of key players. The club opted for a relatively unknown trainer, [Joaquín Caparrós](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joaqu%C3%ADn_Caparr%C3%B3s "Joaquín Caparrós"), who helped the team win the Second Division with three matches to spare in just his first season at the helm.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-39)

### Successes in the 21st century

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sevilla_FC&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Successes in the 21st century")]

In May 2002, Roberto Alés resigned as president, and the Sevillian lawyer José María del Nido assumed the presidency. One of his first decisions was to confirm Caparrós as a coach and [Monchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monchi "Monchi") as sporting director.

[![Image 50](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Sevilla_UEFA_Cup_2006.jpg/250px-Sevilla_UEFA_Cup_2006.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sevilla_UEFA_Cup_2006.jpg)

Players and staff of Sevilla celebrating the [UEFA Cup victory in 2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_UEFA_Cup_Final "2006 UEFA Cup Final")

On 6 October 2002, before a [Seville derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seville_derby "Seville derby") against Betis at the Sánchez Pizjuán, four Sevilla fans, including a minor, assaulted a security guard. The attack was punished by Sevilla being forced to play their next four home matches behind closed doors, the longest term ever given to a La Liga side. The club finished sixth in the [2003–04 La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003%E2%80%9304_La_Liga "2003–04 La Liga"), giving the club qualification for the [2004–05 UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Cup "2004–05 UEFA Cup") and marking a return to continental competition for the first time since the 1995–96 season. In the [2004–05](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_La_Liga "2004–05 La Liga") league season, Sevilla finished sixth and qualified for the [following season's UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_UEFA_Cup "2005–06 UEFA Cup"), entering the competition in the third qualifying round.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-2005_06_un-40)

This set up Sevilla's first-ever European triumph in the [2006 UEFA Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_UEFA_Cup_Final "2006 UEFA Cup Final") at the [Philips Stadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philips_Stadion "Philips Stadion") in [Eindhoven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eindhoven "Eindhoven") on 10 May 2006. The club defeated English club [Middlesbrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlesbrough_F.C. "Middlesbrough F.C.") 4–0 under new manager [Juande Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juande_Ramos "Juande Ramos"), with the scoring opened by Brazilian striker [Luís Fabiano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lu%C3%ADs_Fabiano "Luís Fabiano"). In the second-half, Italian substitute [Enzo Maresca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzo_Maresca "Enzo Maresca") scored twice to be named Man of the Match, and Malian striker [Frédéric Kanouté](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fr%C3%A9d%C3%A9ric_Kanout%C3%A9 "Frédéric Kanouté") finished the scoring, to give the club its first major title in 58 years on the season of its centenary, which was celebrated in October 2005.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-2005_06_un-40)

Sevilla opened their [2006–07 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_La_Liga "2006–07 La Liga") by winning the [2006 UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_UEFA_Super_Cup "2006 UEFA Super Cup") on 25 August 2006 with a 3–0 victory over Champions League winners and compatriots Barcelona at the [Stade Louis II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_Louis_II "Stade Louis II") in Monaco. The goals were scored by [Renato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_(footballer,_born_1979) "Renato (footballer, born 1979)"), Kanouté and a late penalty by Maresca.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-41) The season ended with a second consecutive UEFA Cup win, this time against fellow Spanish club [Espanyol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCD_Espanyol "RCD Espanyol") at [Hampden Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hampden_Park "Hampden Park"), Glasgow.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-42) The match went to penalties after finishing 2–2 after extra-time, with Sevilla goalkeeper [Andrés Palop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_Palop "Andrés Palop") saving three of Espanyol's penalties.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-el_sevilla_cierra-43)

[![Image 51](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/38/Sevilla_F%C3%BAtbol_Club_league_performance_1929-present.svg/250px-Sevilla_F%C3%BAtbol_Club_league_performance_1929-present.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sevilla_F%C3%BAtbol_Club_league_performance_1929-present.svg)

Chart of Sevilla FC league performance 1929–present

On 12 November 2006, Sevilla played its 2,000th game in La Liga. Sevilla defeated [Getafe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getafe_CF "Getafe CF") in the [2007 Copa del Rey Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Copa_del_Rey_Final "2007 Copa del Rey Final"), with Kanouté scoring the only goal in the game's 11th minute. Sevilla finished third in [that season's La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_La_Liga "2006–07 La Liga") to qualify for the [2007–08 Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_UEFA_Champions_League "2007–08 UEFA Champions League"), returning to the competition for the first time in 50 years.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-el_sevilla_cierra-43) As a result of these successes, Sevilla was voted as the [IFFHS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_Football_History_&_Statistics "International Federation of Football History & Statistics") Team of the Year for the second consecutive season, becoming the first club to achieve this.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-:0-10)

Sevilla won the [2007 Supercopa de España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "2007 Supercopa de España") against La Liga champions Real Madrid.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-44) The season started to derail, however, after defender Antonio Puerta suffered a heart attack in the first game of the season and died three days later on 28 August. Three days after his death, Sevilla then lost 3–1 to [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.C._Milan "A.C. Milan") in the [2007 UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_UEFA_Super_Cup "2007 UEFA Super Cup") in Monaco.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-45) Juande Ramos, the individual largely responsible for Sevilla's recent successes, resigned as manager on 27 October to take the post with [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C."); he was replaced by [Sevilla Atlético](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_Atl%C3%A9tico "Sevilla Atlético") manager [Manolo Jiménez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Jim%C3%A9nez_Jim%C3%A9nez "Manuel Jiménez Jiménez").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-46) In spite of the personnel issues, Sevilla nonetheless advanced in first place in its Champions League group ahead of [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") before later being eliminated in the round of 16 via penalties to [Fenerbahçe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenerbah%C3%A7e_S.K._(football) "Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)") of Turkey.

The squad in 2010

In the summer of 2008, before Jiménez's debut season as first-team manager, [Dani Alves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dani_Alves "Dani Alves") and [Seydou Keita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seydou_Keita "Seydou Keita") were both sold to Barcelona, while [Christian Poulsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Poulsen "Christian Poulsen") left for [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC"). Sevilla finished third in La Liga with a club record-equalling 21 victories and a club record number of away victories.

The [2009–10 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_La_Liga "2009–10 La Liga") saw a third-consecutive qualification to the Champions League. On 19 May 2010, Sevilla defeated Atlético Madrid 2–0 in the [2010 Copa del Rey Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Copa_del_Rey_Final "2010 Copa del Rey Final") at [Camp Nou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Nou "Camp Nou"), with goals from [Diego Capel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Capel "Diego Capel") and [Jesús Navas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jes%C3%BAs_Navas "Jesús Navas").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-48) Before the 2010–11 season started, Sevilla lost to Barcelona 5–3 on aggregate in the [Supercopa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "2010 Supercopa de España") and were eliminated in the [Champions League playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_UEFA_Champions_League_qualifying_phase_and_play-off_round "2010–11 UEFA Champions League qualifying phase and play-off round") by Portuguese club [Braga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.C._Braga "S.C. Braga").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-49)

### Unai Emery era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sevilla_FC&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Unai Emery era")]

[![Image 53](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Deporsevilla.jpg/250px-Deporsevilla.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Deporsevilla.jpg)

[Deportivo de La Coruña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deportivo_de_La_Coru%C3%B1a "Deportivo de La Coruña") vs. Sevilla FC.

On 14 January of the following year, after a 0–2 away loss to Valencia that left the Andalusians in 12th place, Jiménez was relieved of his duties, and was replaced by Spanish manager [Unai Emery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unai_Emery "Unai Emery"). The club went through an organizational financial crisis and was forced to sell team stars [Álvaro Negredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81lvaro_Negredo "Álvaro Negredo") and Jesús Navas, transactions that gave the club a combined €40 million; the duo was replaced by a contingent of younger players including strikers [Carlos Bacca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Bacca "Carlos Bacca") and [Kevin Gameiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Gameiro "Kevin Gameiro").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-sevilla_0_0-50)

On 14 May 2014, Sevilla defeated [Benfica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica") on penalties in the [2014 UEFA Europa League Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_UEFA_Europa_League_Final "2014 UEFA Europa League Final") to claim their third triumph in the competition.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-sevilla_0_0-50) After this season key midfielder [Ivan Rakitić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Rakiti%C4%87 "Ivan Rakitić") was sold to Barcelona for around €16 million (the deal was closed on 16 June 2014[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-51)). In summer 2015 top scorer Carlos Bacca, who had only joined two years previous, moved to Milan for €30 million.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-52) Despite these exits, the club acquired players [Grzegorz Krychowiak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grzegorz_Krychowiak "Grzegorz Krychowiak") and [Éver Banega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89ver_Banega "Éver Banega") to reinforce the squad.

On 27 May 2015, Sevilla were again Europa League champions after defeating Ukrainian club [Dnipro Dnipropetrovsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Dnipro_Dnipropetrovsk "FC Dnipro Dnipropetrovsk") 3–2 in the [2015 Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Europa_League_Final "2015 UEFA Europa League Final").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-53) The goals for Sevilla were scored by [Grzegorz Krychowiak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grzegorz_Krychowiak "Grzegorz Krychowiak") and a brace from [Carlos Bacca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Bacca "Carlos Bacca").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-54) By defeating Dnipro, they became the only club to have won the Europa League four times.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-55)

The club returned to the Europa League final for a third consecutive time, facing [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") in the [2016 Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_UEFA_Europa_League_Final "2016 UEFA Europa League Final"). After being down 0–1 at half-time, Sevilla bounced back in the second half to eventually win 3–1, with one goal scored from Kevin Gameiro and two from club captain [Coke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coke_(footballer) "Coke (footballer)"). With its third consecutive Europa League title, Sevilla improved its record of most Europa League titles won, having lifted the trophy five times in the span of ten years.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-uefa.com-56)

### Post-Emery era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sevilla_FC&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Post-Emery era")]

Despite Sevilla's continued success in the Europa League, the [2015–16 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_La_Liga "2015–16 La Liga") proved to be another finish outside the top four, the side finishing in seventh. In response, Castro decided to engineer a resurrection of the club. [Jorge Sampaoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Sampaoli "Jorge Sampaoli") was hired as manager – replacing [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C. "Paris Saint-Germain F.C.")-bound Unai Emery[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-57) – and the club began to invest heavily that summer. Additions to the side included goalkeeper [Salvatore Sirigu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvatore_Sirigu "Salvatore Sirigu") on loan,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-58) playmaker [Ganso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paulo_Henrique_Ganso "Paulo Henrique Ganso"), forward [Luciano Vietto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Vietto "Luciano Vietto") and [Wissam Ben Yedder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wissam_Ben_Yedder "Wissam Ben Yedder"), attacker [Franco Vázquez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco_V%C3%A1zquez "Franco Vázquez"), wide midfielders [Hiroshi Kiyotake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiroshi_Kiyotake "Hiroshi Kiyotake") and [Pablo Sarabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Sarabia "Pablo Sarabia"), as well as former [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") and [Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") player [Samir Nasri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samir_Nasri "Samir Nasri") on loan.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-59)

In December of the [2017–18 La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_La_Liga "2017–18 La Liga"), [Vincenzo Montella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincenzo_Montella "Vincenzo Montella") was named as the third manager since Emery's departure in 2016 replacing Eduardo Berizzo.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-60) In the [2017–18 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_UEFA_Champions_League "2017–18 UEFA Champions League") season, Sevilla progressed into the knockout stages of the competition, and defeated [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United "Manchester United") in the Round of 16,[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-61) reaching the round of 8 for the first time in 60 years, where they ultimately lost to [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") 2–1 on aggregate.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-62)

On 4 June 2019, Sevilla announced the signing of [Julen Lopetegui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julen_Lopetegui "Julen Lopetegui") as manager for the next three seasons.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-63) On 16 August 2020, Sevilla won 2–1 over [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United "Manchester United") in the semi-finals of the [2019–20 UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_UEFA_Europa_League "2019–20 UEFA Europa League"),[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-64) en route to lifting the trophy for a record sixth time, beating [Inter Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan") 3–2 in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Europa_League_Final "2020 UEFA Europa League Final").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-65)

On 31 May 2023, Sevilla clinched their record-extending [7th Europa League title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2023 UEFA Europa League final") with a win over [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.S._Roma "A.S. Roma"), drawing 1–1 after extra time and beating them 4–1 on penalties.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-66)

### Presidency

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sevilla_FC&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Presidency")]

Sevilla is governed by a presidential management system, but with a board of directors that discusses and approves those important decisions that must be carried out. The president is supported by a general director sometimes and a sports director.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-Historia-13)

Throughout its history, Sevilla has had 28 presidents,[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-67) the first being [Edward Farquharson Johnston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Farquharson_Johnston "Edward Farquharson Johnston"), a Scotsman. Those who have occupied the presidency for the longest periods have been Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán, Eugenio Montes Cabezas, José María del Nido Benavente, Luis Cuervas Vilches and José Castro Carmona.

In 1992, Sevilla FC became a Sporting Limited Association, following the entry into force of the law that regulated this kind of sporting companies, and therefore the system of election of the president was amended from being elected by the members to be elected by the shareholders of the club.

### Anthems

[![Image 54](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Elarrebato_20m.jpg/250px-Elarrebato_20m.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Elarrebato_20m.jpg)

El Arrebato, author and interpreter of the Centennial Anthem

Sevilla has two official anthems:

*   **Official Anthem of Sevilla FC:** This anthem dates back to the year 1983. The lyrics were written by Ángel Luis Osquiguilea de Roncales and the music was composed by Manuel Osquiguilea de Roncales.
*   **Centennial Anthem of Sevilla FC:** Composed in 2005 by singer Javier Labandón 'El Arrebato' to commemorate the centenary of the registration of the club's articles of association, it became Spain's number one single and the best-selling anthem of a football club in the entire history of Spanish football, reaching the 2nd position of the best-selling albums in 2006.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-69) On 9 October 2006, in the Estadio Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, 'El Arrebato' was awarded the golden record his anthem.

### Crest

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sevilla_FC&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Crest")]

From its foundation, the team used a double-circled crest. On the exterior circle, the name of the club and the date of its foundation were written, while in the interior circle on a white background the letters "SFC" were interlaced as they are on the current crest.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-70) This first crest was designed by Juan Lafita, who was a close associate of the club and was the son of the Sevillian painter José Lafita y Blanco.

The second crest was designed in 1922 by Pablo Rodríguez Blanco, a draftsman of the Water Company. He divided the shield in three parts and together they formed the silhouette of a heart. The three figures that appear are the Christian saints portrayed on the coat of arms of the city – [Isidore of Seville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isidore_of_Seville "Isidore of Seville"), [Ferdinand III of Castile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_III_of_Castile "Ferdinand III of Castile") and [Leander of Seville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leander_of_Seville "Leander of Seville"). On the right side appear the initials "SFC," which were on the official shield from 1905 to 1922.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-71)

Where the three parts meet, a football of the era appears. Regarding the red and white stripes, there are various theories, but it seems that the most coherent is that from the first time, the club wished that the official kit would be red and white. Another version indicates that the lower part is inspired on the flag which King [Ferdinand III of Castile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_III_of_Castile "Ferdinand III of Castile") carried in the reconquest of Seville in 1248.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC#cite_note-Historia-13)

### Flag

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sevilla_FC&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Flag")]

The definition of Sevilla's flag is in the articles of association of 1982, which is a modification of the old ones which were formed and deposited in the Record of Associations and Sports Federations of the Higher Council of Sports. Its title 1, article 6 states that this is a distinctive emblem of the club:

The flag, which will be rectangular, divided by a diagonal line that goes from the lower left angle to the upper right angle, which divides it into two triangles, the superior is white and the inferior red.

### Media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sevilla_FC&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Media")]

Sevilla have several media outlets. Its radio station, _SFC Radio_, launched in September 2004, broadcasts all day on FM and online, while its television channel SFC TV aired for the first time in the 2005–06 season with a UEFA Cup match against [Zenit Saint Petersburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Zenit_Saint_Petersburg "FC Zenit Saint Petersburg"). Since 8 June 2009, the television coverage has been shown on the club website. Sevilla issue a physical and digital newspaper the day after every match and on the same day as an important one, as well as a magazine before home games. The official magazine of the club is released every two months, the first issue being free and issued at a friendly against the [Brazil national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") to mark the club's centennial in September 2005.
