After another three seasons in the second division, with the club managed by [Lorenzo Serra Ferrer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenzo_Serra_Ferrer "Lorenzo Serra Ferrer"), Betis [returned to the top flight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993%E2%80%9394_Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n "1993–94 Segunda División") for the [1994–95 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994%E2%80%9395_La_Liga "1994–95 La Liga"), subsequently achieving a final third position, thus [qualifying to the UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995%E2%80%9396_UEFA_Cup "1995–96 UEFA Cup").

[![Image 48](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/Camiseta_aniversario_betis_001.jpg/250px-Camiseta_aniversario_betis_001.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Camiseta_aniversario_betis_001.jpg)

Betis' shirts in 2007 bore an emblem for their centenary.

In the European campaign, Betis knocked out [Fenerbahçe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenerbah%C3%A7e_S.K._(football) "Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)") (4–1 on aggregate) and [1. FC Kaiserslautern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1._FC_Kaiserslautern "1. FC Kaiserslautern") (4–1) before losing to [defeated finalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_UEFA_Cup_Final "1996 UEFA Cup Final")[Bordeaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Girondins_de_Bordeaux "FC Girondins de Bordeaux") (3–2). In 1997, 20 years after winning the trophy for the first time, the club returned to the final of the Copa del Rey – again held in Madrid, although this time at the [Santiago Bernabéu Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium") – [losing 2–3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_Copa_del_Rey_Final "1997 Copa del Rey Final") against [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") after [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports) "Overtime (sports)").

Incidentally, _Barça_ was the club Serra Ferrer would leave Betis for that summer, to be replaced by former player [Luis Aragonés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Aragon%C3%A9s "Luis Aragonés"). Aragonés would only last [one season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997%E2%80%9398_La_Liga "1997–98 La Liga") with the club, leading the side to the eighth position and to [the quarter-finals in the Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997%E2%80%9398_UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup "1997–98 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup"), where they would lose 2–5 on aggregate to eventual winners [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.").

Aragonés was followed by the controversial reign of [Javier Clemente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javier_Clemente "Javier Clemente"), who spat on a fan and implied Andalusia was "another country!".[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The team slipped down the table, [finishing 11th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998%E2%80%9399_La_Liga "1998–99 La Liga") and [being knocked out of the UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998%E2%80%9399_UEFA_Cup "1998–99 UEFA Cup") by [Bologna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bologna_F.C._1909 "Bologna F.C. 1909") in the third round. For the next couple of seasons, Betis went through numerous managers, a relegation and a promotion, after which the team [finished sixth in the league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001%E2%80%9302_La_Liga "2001–02 La Liga") with [Juande Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juande_Ramos "Juande Ramos") at the helm.

Ramos was gone after just one season, however, being replaced by former Cup Winners' Cup-winning manager [Víctor Fernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V%C3%ADctor_Fern%C3%A1ndez "Víctor Fernández"). He led the team to [eighth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002%E2%80%9303_La_Liga "2002–03 La Liga") and [ninth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003%E2%80%9304_La_Liga "2003–04 La Liga") in the league and the [third round of the 2002–03 UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002%E2%80%9303_UEFA_Cup "2002–03 UEFA Cup"), being knocked out by [Auxerre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AJ_Auxerre "AJ Auxerre") (1–2 on aggregate), during his two-year reign.

For 2004, Fernández was replaced by the returning Serra Ferrer, who guided the team to the [fourth position in the top flight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_La_Liga "2004–05 La Liga"). They also returned to the Vicente Calderón on 11 June 2005 for the [Copa del Rey final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Copa_del_Rey "2004–05 Copa del Rey"), lifting the trophy for only the second time after an extra-time winner by youth graduate [Dani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dani_(footballer,_born_1981) "Dani (footballer, born 1981)") in a [2–1 win](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Copa_del_Rey_Final "2005 Copa del Rey Final") against [Osasuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CA_Osasuna "CA Osasuna").

The league finish meant Betis became the first Andalusian team to compete in the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"), and it reached [the group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_UEFA_Champions_League "2005–06 UEFA Champions League") after disposing of [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Monaco_FC "AS Monaco FC") in the last qualifying round (3–2 on aggregate). Drawn in Group G, and in spite of a 1–0 home win against Chelsea,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-10) the club eventually finished third, being "demoted" to the [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_UEFA_Cup "2005–06 UEFA Cup"), where it would be ousted in the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_UEFA_Cup_knockout_stage "2005–06 UEFA Cup knockout stage") by Romanian club [Steaua București](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Steaua_Bucure%C8%99ti "FC Steaua București") with a 0–3 home loss.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-11) Compared to the previous season, the [league campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_La_Liga "2005–06 La Liga") was disappointing, with the club finishing in 14th place, just three points off the relegation zone.

### Centenary celebrations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Centenary celebrations")]

[![Image 49](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Rgordillo.jpg/250px-Rgordillo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rgordillo.jpg)

[Rafael Gordillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Gordillo "Rafael Gordillo"), Betis player and president

Betis celebrated their [centenary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Century "Century") year in 2007. The festivities included a special match against Milan, the [reigning European Champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2007 UEFA Champions League Final"), on August 9, with the hosts winning 1–0 thanks to a [Mark González](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Gonz%C3%A1lez "Mark González")[penalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kick_(association_football) "Penalty kick (association football)") early in the second half. Seven days later, the club won the [Ramón de Carranza Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_de_Carranza_Trophy "Ramón de Carranza Trophy") held in neighbouring [Cádiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A1diz "Cádiz"), beating [Real Zaragoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Zaragoza "Real Zaragoza") on penalties in the final, having defeated Real Madrid in the semi-finals.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-12)

Surrounding the celebration, it was a time of great change in terms of the playing and technical teams, with eight new signings replacing 14 departures. In the summer of 2006, Serra Ferrer was replaced by [Luis Fernandez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Fernandez "Luis Fernandez") for the [2006–07](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_La_Liga "2006–07 La Liga") season. However, the two seasons that encompassed the centenary year (2006–07 and [2007–08](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Real_Betis_season "2007–08 Real Betis season")) were disappointing, with the club having four different managers and barely avoiding relegation in both seasons.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-13)

### Relegation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Relegation")]

After many years of staving off relegation, Betis' [2008–09 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Real_Betis_season "2008–09 Real Betis season") culminated with a 1–1 draw against [Real Valladolid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Valladolid "Real Valladolid") at home. As a result, the club finished 18th in the table and consequently was relegated to the second division on goal difference.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-14)

On 15 June 2009 over 65,000 _Beticos_, including icons such as [Rafael Gordillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Gordillo "Rafael Gordillo"), Del Sol, [Hipólito Rincón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip%C3%B3lito_Rinc%C3%B3n "Hipólito Rincón"), [Julio Cardeñosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julio_Carde%C3%B1osa "Julio Cardeñosa") and others, joined the protest march in Sevilla with the slogan "_15-J Yo Voy Betis_" to let the majority owner Ruiz de Lopera know that it was time to put his 54% share of the club on the market for someone, some entity or the Betis supporters to buy those shares and remove Lopera from the day-to-day operations of the club.

Despite the protests, no upper management changes were made during [the season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n "2009–10 Segunda División"), which would ultimately see Betis fail to gain promotion back to the top level.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-15)

### Lopera court action and sale

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Lopera court action and sale")]

Seville judge Mercedes Alaya was investigating links between Betis and other Ruiz de Lopera-owned businesses, leading to him being formally charged with fraud. On 7 July 2010, one week before the start of preliminary court proceedings, Lopera sold 94% of the shares that he owned (51% of Betis total shares) to Bitton Sport, fronted by Luis Oliver, for the surprisingly low figure of €16 million, leaving Lopera with only minor shares; Oliver had already reportedly taken two football clubs, [Cartagena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartagena_FC "Cartagena FC") and [Xerez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xerez_CD "Xerez CD"), to the brink of bankruptcy.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-16)

Before the sale could be officially sanctioned, however, Ayala froze Lopera shareholdings. Left with nothing, despite putting down a €1 million deposit, Oliver hastily bought a nominal number of shares from a third party and was voted onto the board of directors by the existing members (all former cohorts of Lopera), allowing him to carry on running the club. In response to this, the judge appointed well-respected former Betis, Real Madrid and Spain national team legend [Rafael Gordillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Gordillo "Rafael Gordillo") to administer Lopera's shares to ensure Lopera was not still running the club and that decisions made were for the benefit of the club not individual board members.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-17)

Again under [Pepe Mel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_Mel "Pepe Mel"), Betis started [2011–12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_La_Liga "2011–12 La Liga") with four wins in as many games, with [Rubén Castro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rub%C3%A9n_Castro "Rubén Castro") retaining his goal scoring form from [the previous season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n "2010–11 Segunda División"), where he scored 27 goals. In the [2012–13 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_La_Liga "2012–13 La Liga"), Betis finished seventh in La Liga and qualified for the [2013–14 UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Europa_League "2013–14 UEFA Europa League"), the first European qualification for the club since the [2005–06 Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_UEFA_Champions_League "2005–06 UEFA Champions League"). This European campaign ended in the quarter-finals after losing on penalties to local rivals Sevilla.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-18) Betis were relegated from La Liga with three games still to play in the [2013–14 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_La_Liga "2013–14 La Liga"),[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-19) but [returned immediately as champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n "2014–15 Segunda División") with two games to spare.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-20)

In the [2017–18 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Real_Betis_season "2017–18 Real Betis season"), under [Quique Setién](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quique_Seti%C3%A9n "Quique Setién"), Betis finished sixth in La Liga and earned a spot in the Europa League. The 2018–19 campaign was very positive; the club reached the [Copa del Rey semi-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Copa_del_Rey "2018–19 Copa del Rey") and topped their group in the Europa League, before eventually being knocked out by [Stade Rennais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_Rennais_F.C. "Stade Rennais F.C.") in the [round of 32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Europa_League_knockout_phase "2018–19 UEFA Europa League knockout phase").

On 9 July 2020, [Manuel Pellegrini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Pellegrini "Manuel Pellegrini") was appointed as Betis manager ahead of the 2020–21 season. He guided them to a sixth-place finish and a Europa League spot, an improvement from 15th the previous season.

Betis won the [Copa del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Copa_del_Rey "2021–22 Copa del Rey") final against [Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia_CF "Valencia CF") after drawing 1–1 after 120 minutes and winning 5–4 on penalties. It was the first trophy for 17 years, since the [2005 edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Copa_del_Rey "2004–05 Copa del Rey").

The club displayed consistency under Pellegrini's management by qualifying for the [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League") for three consecutive seasons, finishing fifth and sixth in the [2021–22](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_La_Liga "2021–22 La Liga") and [2022–23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_La_Liga "2022–23 La Liga") seasons, respectively. The club qualified for the [Conference League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_UEFA_Conference_League "2024–25 UEFA Conference League") after a seventh-place finish in [2023–24 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_La_Liga "2023–24 La Liga") and reached the club's first ever European final the [following season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_UEFA_Conference_League "2024–25 UEFA Conference League"). However, they [lost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_UEFA_Conference_League_final "2025 UEFA Conference League final") to [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") 1–4.

Betis was able to qualify for the UEFA Champions League for the first time in twenty years following their 5th place finish in the [2025–26 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_La_Liga "2025–26 La Liga").

## Seville derby

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Seville derby")]

[![Image 53](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Regatsasevillabetis2009.JPG/250px-Regatsasevillabetis2009.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Regatsasevillabetis2009.JPG)

Betis and their city rival, Sevilla FC, also compete in an annual rowing race on the [Guadalquivir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalquivir "Guadalquivir") river.

See also: [El derbi Sevillano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_derbi_Sevillano "El derbi Sevillano")

Betis have a long-standing rivalry with city neighbours Sevilla FC.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-BETIS-5) The two have met 114 times in official competition, with Sevilla holding a 45% win ratio over Betis (31%).

The first match between the two clubs took place on 8 February 1915, with Sevilla winning 4–3. The match was not completed, as high tensions led an aggressive crowd to invade the pitch, forcing the [referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referee_(association_football) "Referee (association football)") to abandon the match.

In 1916, the first [Copa Andalucía](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Andaluc%C3%ADa "Copa Andalucía") was held, this being the first official derby of the Sevilla area. Of the 17 runnings of the cup, Sevilla were victorious 14 times, to Betis' one sole conquest; this included a 22–0 routing after the latter sent their youth team, in 1918.

The first time the teams met in league, in _Segunda_, happened in 1928–29, with both teams winning their home matches (3–0 and 2–1). They played for the first time in the Spanish top division during the 1934–35 season, with a 0–3 home defeat for Sevilla and a 2–2 draw at Betis, with the latter winning the national championship.

On 17 January 1943, Betis lost 5–0 at Sevilla, eventually being relegated. In the first game held at the [Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_S%C3%A1nchez_Pizju%C3%A1n_Stadium "Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium"), on 21 September 1958, the _Verdiblancos_ won it 4–2.

In later years, several matches were also marred by violence, including: a security guard attacked by a Sevilla fan with a crutch (that he did not require to walk), Betis [goalkeeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goalkeeper_(association_football) "Goalkeeper (association football)")[Toni Prats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Prats_Cervera "Antonio Prats Cervera") being attacked and Sevilla manager Juande Ramos being struck by a bottle of water;[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-21) the latter incident led to the [2007 Copa del Rey match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_Copa_del_Rey "2006–07 Copa del Rey") being suspended, being played out three weeks later in [Getafe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getafe "Getafe") with no spectators.

On 7 February 2009 Betis won 2–1 at the Pizjuán, but was eventually relegated from the top flight, while Sevilla finished in third position.

On 9 November 2019 more than 10,000 Betis fans visited the team training before the last derby in 2019.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-22)

**Real Betis Balompié, S.A.D.**, known as **Real Betis** (pronounced[[reˈal ˈbetis]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish")), is a professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in [Seville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seville "Seville"), [Andalusia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andalusia "Andalusia"), Spain. They compete in [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga"), the [top flight of Spanish football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_football_league_system "Spanish football league system"). Traditionally, Real Betis play home matches at [Estadio Benito Villamarín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_Benito_Villamar%C3%ADn "Estadio Benito Villamarín"). However, since 2025, the club have played their home games at the 70,000-seat [Estadio La Cartuja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_La_Cartuja "Estadio La Cartuja") while awaiting the completion of a €262 million redevelopment of their traditional home.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-4)

Real Betis won the league title in [1935](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1934%E2%80%9335_La_Liga "1934–35 La Liga") and the [Copa del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey "Copa del Rey") in [1977](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_Copa_del_Rey "1976–77 Copa del Rey"), [2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Copa_del_Rey "2004–05 Copa del Rey") and [2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Copa_del_Rey "2021–22 Copa del Rey"). Given the club's tumultuous history and many relegations, its motto is _¡Viva el Betis manque pierda!_ (_Long live Betis even when they lose!_).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-BETIS-5)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [History of Real Betis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Real_Betis "History of Real Betis")

The name "Betis" is derived from _[Baetis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispania\_Baetica "Hispania Baetica")_, the Roman name for the [Guadalquivir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalquivir "Guadalquivir") river which passes through Seville and which the Roman province there was named after. _Real_ ('Royal') was added in 1914 after the club received patronage from King [Alfonso XIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfonso_XIII "Alfonso XIII").

### Foundation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Foundation")]

[![Image 43](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Alineaci%C3%B3n_del_Real_Betis_Balompie%2C_1913..jpg/250px-Alineaci%C3%B3n_del_Real_Betis_Balompie%2C_1913..jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Alineaci%C3%B3n_del_Real_Betis_Balompie,_1913..jpg)

Real Betis, 25 December 1913

[![Image 44](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/83/Estadio_Exposici%C3%B3n_1929.jpg/250px-Estadio_Exposici%C3%B3n_1929.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Estadio_Exposici%C3%B3n_1929.jpg)

The grounds of the Estadio de la Exposición (now Benito Villamarín) in 1929

Betis' city rivals Sevilla were the first club in Seville, founded in October 1905, while a second club, _España Balompié_ were established in September 1907. "_Balompié_" translates literally as "football", as opposed to the most commonly adopted anglicised version, "_fútbol_". Balompié was founded by students from the local Polytechnic Academy, and were in operation for one year before being officially recognised in 1909 as _Sevilla Balompié_; despite this, 1907 remains the official foundation date of the club.

Following an internal split from Sevilla FC, another club was formed, Betis Football Club. In 1914, they merged with Sevilla Balompié. The club received its royal patronage in the same year, and therefore adopted the name **Real Betis Balompié**. Fans continued to refer to the club as _Balompié_ and were themselves known as _Los Balompedistas_ until the 1930s, when _Betis_ and the adjective _Béticos_ became common terminology when discussing the club and its followers.

Real Betis originally played in all blue jerseys and white shorts, for no other reason than the easy availability of such plain colours.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] However, one of the club's founders and team captain, Manuel Ramos Asensio, was keen to take advantage of his relationships made while studying in Scotland, contacted the Irish-founded Scottish club [Celtic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_F.C. "Celtic F.C."), whose green and white colours matched the Andalusian regional flag, and obtained the same fabric Celtic used to make kits for his own club. Celtic originally wore green and white stripes but had reoriented a few years earlier to horizontal hoops. Ramos opted for vertical stripes to make the shirts as no other Spanish club used the combination at the time. In 2017 the club officially acknowledged the link with Celtic by producing a special hooped kit to coincide with [Andalusia Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andalusia_Day "Andalusia Day").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-6) The blue colour is still often used in away kit designs.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-7)

### 1930s: promotion, championship and relegation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1930s: promotion, championship and relegation")]

During the [Spanish Second Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Second_Republic "Spanish Second Republic") (1931–1939), royal patronage of all organisations was nullified, and thus the club was known as **Betis Balompié** until after the [Spanish Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War "Spanish Civil War") when it would revert to the full name. The club reached the [Copa del Presidente de la República](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey "Copa del Rey") final for the first time on 21 June 1931, when it lost 3–1 to [Athletic Bilbao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletic_Bilbao "Athletic Bilbao") in Madrid.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-8) Betis marked their 25th anniversary year by winning their first [Segunda División](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n "Segunda División") title in [1932](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1931%E2%80%9332_Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n "1931–32 Segunda División"), finishing two points ahead of [Real Oviedo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Oviedo "Real Oviedo"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-9) thus becoming the first club from [Andalusia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andalusia "Andalusia") to play in [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga").

On 28 April 1935, under the guidance of Irish coach [Patrick O'Connell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_O'Connell_(footballer) "Patrick O'Connell (footballer)"), Betis won [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1934%E2%80%9335_La_Liga "1934–35 La Liga"), to date their only top division title. They topped the table by a single point over [Madrid FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_C.F. "Real Madrid C.F."). A year later Betis went down to [seventh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1935%E2%80%9336_La_Liga "1935–36 La Liga"). This was due to the dismantling of the championship-winning team because of the club's poor economic situation and the arrival of the Civil War, meaning that just 15 months after winning the league title only two players who won in 1935 were left: Peral and Saro. No official league was held during the Civil War between 1936 and 1939, until its resumption for the 1939–40 season and the first year back highlighted Betis' decline as exactly five years after winning the title the club was [relegated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1939%E2%80%9340_La_Liga "1939–40 La Liga").

### Darkest period

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Darkest period")]

Despite a brief [return to the top division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1942%E2%80%9343_La_Liga "1942–43 La Liga") which lasted only one season, the club continued to decline and in 1947 an all-time low was reached when the club were relegated to [Tercera División](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tercera_Divisi%C3%B3n "Tercera División"). Many fans see the ten years they spent in the category as key to the "identity" and "soul" of the club. During this time, Betis earned a reputation for filling its stadium and having massive support at away matches, known as the "Green March".[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

When the side returned to the second level in 1954, it gained the distinction of being the only club in Spain to have won all three major divisions' titles. Much of the credit for guiding Betis through this dark period and back into the _Segunda_ lies with chairman Manuel Ruiz Rodríguez.

### Benito Villamarín

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Benito Villamarín")]

In 1955, Manuel Ruiz Rodríguez stepped down from running the club believing he could not offer further economic growth, he was replaced by Betis most famous former president, Benito Villamarín. During his reign Betis returned to the top division in [1958–59](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958%E2%80%9359_La_Liga "1958–59 La Liga") and finished in third place in [1964](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1963%E2%80%9364_La_Liga "1963–64 La Liga"). His purchase of the [Estadio Heliópolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_Benito_Villamar%C3%ADn "Estadio Benito Villamarín") in 1961 is seen as a key point in the history of the club – the grounds were named after him as _Estadio Benito Villamarín_. In 1965, Villamarín stepped down from his position after ten years at the helm of the club.

Just one year after Villamarín's departure, the club would again be relegated to division two, then rising and falling almost consecutively until consolidating their place in the top level in [1974–75](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_La_Liga "1974–75 La Liga").

### First Copa del Rey Title and European Qualification

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: First Copa del Rey Title and European Qualification")]

[![Image 45](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/Manolo_Diaz_en_el_Betis_1_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Manolo_Diaz_en_el_Betis_1_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Manolo_Diaz_en_el_Betis_1_(cropped).jpg)

1974–75 Real Betis squad

On 25 June 1977, Betis played Athletic Bilbao at the [Vicente Calderón Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vicente_Calder%C3%B3n_Stadium "Vicente Calderón Stadium") in the [Copa del Rey final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_Copa_del_Rey#Final "1976–77 Copa del Rey"). The match finished 2–2, with Betis winning 8–7 after a staggering 21 [penalties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shootout_(association_football) "Penalty shootout (association football)") taken to win its first ever Copa del Rey title. This rounded off a solid season in which the club [finished fifth in the league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_La_Liga "1976–77 La Liga").

After that triumph, Betis [competed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977%E2%80%9378_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup "1977–78 European Cup Winners' Cup") in the [European Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup "UEFA Cup Winners' Cup"): after knocking out [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.C._Milan "A.C. Milan") 3–2 on aggregate in the first round, the side reached the quarter-finals, where they lost to [Dynamo Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Dynamo_Moscow "FC Dynamo Moscow"). Despite their strong performance in [Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA"), the team [suffered league relegation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977%E2%80%9378_La_Liga "1977–78 La Liga").

The following year, Betis returned to the top flight and ushered in a period of "good times" for the club, with the next three seasons seeing three top-six finishes, as well as [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League") qualification in [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981%E2%80%9382_La_Liga "1981–82 La Liga") and [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983%E2%80%9384_La_Liga "1983–84 La Liga").

During the summer of 1982, the Benito Villamarín hosted two matches as part of the [1982 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup "1982 FIFA World Cup"), and also witnessed the [Spain national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_national_football_team "Spain national football team")'s famous [12–1 hammering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_vs_Malta_1984_UEFA_European_Football_Championship_qualifying_match "Spain vs Malta 1984 UEFA European Football Championship qualifying match") of [Malta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta_national_football_team "Malta national football team") to [qualify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_1984_qualifying "UEFA Euro 1984 qualifying") for [UEFA Euro 1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_1984 "UEFA Euro 1984").

### Economic crisis and Manuel Ruiz de Lopera

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Economic crisis and Manuel Ruiz de Lopera")]

[![Image 46](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Real_Betis_Balompi%C3%A9_league_performance_1929-present.svg/250px-Real_Betis_Balompi%C3%A9_league_performance_1929-present.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Real_Betis_Balompi%C3%A9_league_performance_1929-present.svg)

Chart of Real Betis league performance 1929–present

In 1992, Betis found itself subject to new league rules and regulations due to its restructuring as an autonomous sporting group (SAD), requiring the club to come up with 1,200 million [pesetas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_peseta "Spanish peseta"), roughly double that of all the first and second division teams, despite being in level two at the time.

In just three months, the fans raised 400 million pesetas with then vice-president [Manuel Ruiz de Lopera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Ruiz_de_Lopera "Manuel Ruiz de Lopera") stepping in to provide an economic guarantee while himself becoming majority shareholder as the team narrowly avoided relegation.

On 11 September 1994, Real Betis played its 1,000th game in La Liga.

### Serra Ferrer success

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Serra Ferrer success")]

After another three seasons in the second division, with the club managed by [Lorenzo Serra Ferrer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenzo_Serra_Ferrer "Lorenzo Serra Ferrer"), Betis [returned to the top flight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993%E2%80%9394_Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n "1993–94 Segunda División") for the [1994–95 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994%E2%80%9395_La_Liga "1994–95 La Liga"), subsequently achieving a final third position, thus [qualifying to the UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995%E2%80%9396_UEFA_Cup "1995–96 UEFA Cup").

[![Image 48](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/Camiseta_aniversario_betis_001.jpg/250px-Camiseta_aniversario_betis_001.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Camiseta_aniversario_betis_001.jpg)

Betis' shirts in 2007 bore an emblem for their centenary.

In the European campaign, Betis knocked out [Fenerbahçe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenerbah%C3%A7e_S.K._(football) "Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)") (4–1 on aggregate) and [1. FC Kaiserslautern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1._FC_Kaiserslautern "1. FC Kaiserslautern") (4–1) before losing to [defeated finalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_UEFA_Cup_Final "1996 UEFA Cup Final")[Bordeaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Girondins_de_Bordeaux "FC Girondins de Bordeaux") (3–2). In 1997, 20 years after winning the trophy for the first time, the club returned to the final of the Copa del Rey – again held in Madrid, although this time at the [Santiago Bernabéu Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium") – [losing 2–3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_Copa_del_Rey_Final "1997 Copa del Rey Final") against [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") after [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports) "Overtime (sports)").

Incidentally, _Barça_ was the club Serra Ferrer would leave Betis for that summer, to be replaced by former player [Luis Aragonés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Aragon%C3%A9s "Luis Aragonés"). Aragonés would only last [one season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997%E2%80%9398_La_Liga "1997–98 La Liga") with the club, leading the side to the eighth position and to [the quarter-finals in the Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997%E2%80%9398_UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup "1997–98 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup"), where they would lose 2–5 on aggregate to eventual winners [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.").

Aragonés was followed by the controversial reign of [Javier Clemente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javier_Clemente "Javier Clemente"), who spat on a fan and implied Andalusia was "another country!".[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The team slipped down the table, [finishing 11th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998%E2%80%9399_La_Liga "1998–99 La Liga") and [being knocked out of the UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998%E2%80%9399_UEFA_Cup "1998–99 UEFA Cup") by [Bologna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bologna_F.C._1909 "Bologna F.C. 1909") in the third round. For the next couple of seasons, Betis went through numerous managers, a relegation and a promotion, after which the team [finished sixth in the league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001%E2%80%9302_La_Liga "2001–02 La Liga") with [Juande Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juande_Ramos "Juande Ramos") at the helm.

Ramos was gone after just one season, however, being replaced by former Cup Winners' Cup-winning manager [Víctor Fernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V%C3%ADctor_Fern%C3%A1ndez "Víctor Fernández"). He led the team to [eighth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002%E2%80%9303_La_Liga "2002–03 La Liga") and [ninth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003%E2%80%9304_La_Liga "2003–04 La Liga") in the league and the [third round of the 2002–03 UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002%E2%80%9303_UEFA_Cup "2002–03 UEFA Cup"), being knocked out by [Auxerre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AJ_Auxerre "AJ Auxerre") (1–2 on aggregate), during his two-year reign.

For 2004, Fernández was replaced by the returning Serra Ferrer, who guided the team to the [fourth position in the top flight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_La_Liga "2004–05 La Liga"). They also returned to the Vicente Calderón on 11 June 2005 for the [Copa del Rey final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Copa_del_Rey "2004–05 Copa del Rey"), lifting the trophy for only the second time after an extra-time winner by youth graduate [Dani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dani_(footballer,_born_1981) "Dani (footballer, born 1981)") in a [2–1 win](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Copa_del_Rey_Final "2005 Copa del Rey Final") against [Osasuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CA_Osasuna "CA Osasuna").

The league finish meant Betis became the first Andalusian team to compete in the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"), and it reached [the group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_UEFA_Champions_League "2005–06 UEFA Champions League") after disposing of [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Monaco_FC "AS Monaco FC") in the last qualifying round (3–2 on aggregate). Drawn in Group G, and in spite of a 1–0 home win against Chelsea,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-10) the club eventually finished third, being "demoted" to the [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_UEFA_Cup "2005–06 UEFA Cup"), where it would be ousted in the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_UEFA_Cup_knockout_stage "2005–06 UEFA Cup knockout stage") by Romanian club [Steaua București](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Steaua_Bucure%C8%99ti "FC Steaua București") with a 0–3 home loss.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-11) Compared to the previous season, the [league campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_La_Liga "2005–06 La Liga") was disappointing, with the club finishing in 14th place, just three points off the relegation zone.

### Centenary celebrations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Centenary celebrations")]

[![Image 49](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Rgordillo.jpg/250px-Rgordillo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rgordillo.jpg)

[Rafael Gordillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Gordillo "Rafael Gordillo"), Betis player and president

Betis celebrated their [centenary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Century "Century") year in 2007. The festivities included a special match against Milan, the [reigning European Champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2007 UEFA Champions League Final"), on August 9, with the hosts winning 1–0 thanks to a [Mark González](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Gonz%C3%A1lez "Mark González")[penalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kick_(association_football) "Penalty kick (association football)") early in the second half. Seven days later, the club won the [Ramón de Carranza Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_de_Carranza_Trophy "Ramón de Carranza Trophy") held in neighbouring [Cádiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A1diz "Cádiz"), beating [Real Zaragoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Zaragoza "Real Zaragoza") on penalties in the final, having defeated Real Madrid in the semi-finals.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-12)

Surrounding the celebration, it was a time of great change in terms of the playing and technical teams, with eight new signings replacing 14 departures. In the summer of 2006, Serra Ferrer was replaced by [Luis Fernandez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Fernandez "Luis Fernandez") for the [2006–07](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_La_Liga "2006–07 La Liga") season. However, the two seasons that encompassed the centenary year (2006–07 and [2007–08](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Real_Betis_season "2007–08 Real Betis season")) were disappointing, with the club having four different managers and barely avoiding relegation in both seasons.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-13)

### Relegation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Relegation")]

After many years of staving off relegation, Betis' [2008–09 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Real_Betis_season "2008–09 Real Betis season") culminated with a 1–1 draw against [Real Valladolid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Valladolid "Real Valladolid") at home. As a result, the club finished 18th in the table and consequently was relegated to the second division on goal difference.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-14)

On 15 June 2009 over 65,000 _Beticos_, including icons such as [Rafael Gordillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Gordillo "Rafael Gordillo"), Del Sol, [Hipólito Rincón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip%C3%B3lito_Rinc%C3%B3n "Hipólito Rincón"), [Julio Cardeñosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julio_Carde%C3%B1osa "Julio Cardeñosa") and others, joined the protest march in Sevilla with the slogan "_15-J Yo Voy Betis_" to let the majority owner Ruiz de Lopera know that it was time to put his 54% share of the club on the market for someone, some entity or the Betis supporters to buy those shares and remove Lopera from the day-to-day operations of the club.

Despite the protests, no upper management changes were made during [the season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n "2009–10 Segunda División"), which would ultimately see Betis fail to gain promotion back to the top level.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-15)

### Lopera court action and sale

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Lopera court action and sale")]

Seville judge Mercedes Alaya was investigating links between Betis and other Ruiz de Lopera-owned businesses, leading to him being formally charged with fraud. On 7 July 2010, one week before the start of preliminary court proceedings, Lopera sold 94% of the shares that he owned (51% of Betis total shares) to Bitton Sport, fronted by Luis Oliver, for the surprisingly low figure of €16 million, leaving Lopera with only minor shares; Oliver had already reportedly taken two football clubs, [Cartagena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartagena_FC "Cartagena FC") and [Xerez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xerez_CD "Xerez CD"), to the brink of bankruptcy.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-16)

Before the sale could be officially sanctioned, however, Ayala froze Lopera shareholdings. Left with nothing, despite putting down a €1 million deposit, Oliver hastily bought a nominal number of shares from a third party and was voted onto the board of directors by the existing members (all former cohorts of Lopera), allowing him to carry on running the club. In response to this, the judge appointed well-respected former Betis, Real Madrid and Spain national team legend [Rafael Gordillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Gordillo "Rafael Gordillo") to administer Lopera's shares to ensure Lopera was not still running the club and that decisions made were for the benefit of the club not individual board members.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-17)

Again under [Pepe Mel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_Mel "Pepe Mel"), Betis started [2011–12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_La_Liga "2011–12 La Liga") with four wins in as many games, with [Rubén Castro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rub%C3%A9n_Castro "Rubén Castro") retaining his goal scoring form from [the previous season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n "2010–11 Segunda División"), where he scored 27 goals. In the [2012–13 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_La_Liga "2012–13 La Liga"), Betis finished seventh in La Liga and qualified for the [2013–14 UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Europa_League "2013–14 UEFA Europa League"), the first European qualification for the club since the [2005–06 Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_UEFA_Champions_League "2005–06 UEFA Champions League"). This European campaign ended in the quarter-finals after losing on penalties to local rivals Sevilla.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-18) Betis were relegated from La Liga with three games still to play in the [2013–14 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_La_Liga "2013–14 La Liga"),[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-19) but [returned immediately as champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n "2014–15 Segunda División") with two games to spare.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-20)

In the [2017–18 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Real_Betis_season "2017–18 Real Betis season"), under [Quique Setién](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quique_Seti%C3%A9n "Quique Setién"), Betis finished sixth in La Liga and earned a spot in the Europa League. The 2018–19 campaign was very positive; the club reached the [Copa del Rey semi-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Copa_del_Rey "2018–19 Copa del Rey") and topped their group in the Europa League, before eventually being knocked out by [Stade Rennais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_Rennais_F.C. "Stade Rennais F.C.") in the [round of 32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Europa_League_knockout_phase "2018–19 UEFA Europa League knockout phase").

On 9 July 2020, [Manuel Pellegrini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Pellegrini "Manuel Pellegrini") was appointed as Betis manager ahead of the 2020–21 season. He guided them to a sixth-place finish and a Europa League spot, an improvement from 15th the previous season.

Betis won the [Copa del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Copa_del_Rey "2021–22 Copa del Rey") final against [Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia_CF "Valencia CF") after drawing 1–1 after 120 minutes and winning 5–4 on penalties. It was the first trophy for 17 years, since the [2005 edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Copa_del_Rey "2004–05 Copa del Rey").

The club displayed consistency under Pellegrini's management by qualifying for the [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League") for three consecutive seasons, finishing fifth and sixth in the [2021–22](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_La_Liga "2021–22 La Liga") and [2022–23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_La_Liga "2022–23 La Liga") seasons, respectively. The club qualified for the [Conference League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_UEFA_Conference_League "2024–25 UEFA Conference League") after a seventh-place finish in [2023–24 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_La_Liga "2023–24 La Liga") and reached the club's first ever European final the [following season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_UEFA_Conference_League "2024–25 UEFA Conference League"). However, they [lost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_UEFA_Conference_League_final "2025 UEFA Conference League final") to [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") 1–4.

Betis was able to qualify for the UEFA Champions League for the first time in twenty years following their 5th place finish in the [2025–26 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_La_Liga "2025–26 La Liga").

## Seville derby

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Real_Betis&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Seville derby")]

[![Image 53](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Regatsasevillabetis2009.JPG/250px-Regatsasevillabetis2009.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Regatsasevillabetis2009.JPG)

Betis and their city rival, Sevilla FC, also compete in an annual rowing race on the [Guadalquivir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalquivir "Guadalquivir") river.

See also: [El derbi Sevillano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_derbi_Sevillano "El derbi Sevillano")

Betis have a long-standing rivalry with city neighbours Sevilla FC.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-BETIS-5) The two have met 114 times in official competition, with Sevilla holding a 45% win ratio over Betis (31%).

The first match between the two clubs took place on 8 February 1915, with Sevilla winning 4–3. The match was not completed, as high tensions led an aggressive crowd to invade the pitch, forcing the [referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referee_(association_football) "Referee (association football)") to abandon the match.

In 1916, the first [Copa Andalucía](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Andaluc%C3%ADa "Copa Andalucía") was held, this being the first official derby of the Sevilla area. Of the 17 runnings of the cup, Sevilla were victorious 14 times, to Betis' one sole conquest; this included a 22–0 routing after the latter sent their youth team, in 1918.

The first time the teams met in league, in _Segunda_, happened in 1928–29, with both teams winning their home matches (3–0 and 2–1). They played for the first time in the Spanish top division during the 1934–35 season, with a 0–3 home defeat for Sevilla and a 2–2 draw at Betis, with the latter winning the national championship.

On 17 January 1943, Betis lost 5–0 at Sevilla, eventually being relegated. In the first game held at the [Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_S%C3%A1nchez_Pizju%C3%A1n_Stadium "Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium"), on 21 September 1958, the _Verdiblancos_ won it 4–2.

In later years, several matches were also marred by violence, including: a security guard attacked by a Sevilla fan with a crutch (that he did not require to walk), Betis [goalkeeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goalkeeper_(association_football) "Goalkeeper (association football)")[Toni Prats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Prats_Cervera "Antonio Prats Cervera") being attacked and Sevilla manager Juande Ramos being struck by a bottle of water;[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-21) the latter incident led to the [2007 Copa del Rey match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_Copa_del_Rey "2006–07 Copa del Rey") being suspended, being played out three weeks later in [Getafe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getafe "Getafe") with no spectators.

On 7 February 2009 Betis won 2–1 at the Pizjuán, but was eventually relegated from the top flight, while Sevilla finished in third position.

On 9 November 2019 more than 10,000 Betis fans visited the team training before the last derby in 2019.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis#cite_note-22)

## Season summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005%E2%80%9306_Sevilla_FC_season&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Season summary")]

Sevilla came on fifth place in the domestic league with 68 points in total. Fourth-placed [Osasuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CA_Osasuna "CA Osasuna") also got 68 points, but won one more game. In the [Copa del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005-06_Copa_del_Rey "2005-06 Copa del Rey"), the team lost in the round of 16 against [Cádiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A1diz_CF "Cádiz CF"). In the [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005-06_UEFA_Cup "2005-06 UEFA Cup"), the team won their first ever European tournament by defeating [Middlesbrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlesbrough_F.C "Middlesbrough F.C") by 4–0 in the final.

## Season summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005%E2%80%9306_Sevilla_FC_season&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Season summary")]

Sevilla came on fifth place in the domestic league with 68 points in total. Fourth-placed [Osasuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CA_Osasuna "CA Osasuna") also got 68 points, but won one more game. In the [Copa del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005-06_Copa_del_Rey "2005-06 Copa del Rey"), the team lost in the round of 16 against [Cádiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A1diz_CF "Cádiz CF"). In the [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005-06_UEFA_Cup "2005-06 UEFA Cup"), the team won their first ever European tournament by defeating [Middlesbrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlesbrough_F.C "Middlesbrough F.C") by 4–0 in the final.

**Basic Training** or bootcamp is a short intensive program for induction of recruits into an [army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army "Army") or [navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy "Navy"). In the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") a few military bases have special units devoted to basic training. The [jargon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jargon "Jargon") of the service is introduced as well as the fundamentals of military discipline and the recruits are trained in the basic skills of their service. A great deal of emphasis is placed on proper wearing of the uniform, grooming, and drill.

Army recruits are often instructed in the firing and care of [guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun "Gun"); Navy recruits get a short introduction to [fire fighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire_fighting "Fire fighting").

See [saltpetre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saltpetre "Saltpetre")

**Basic Training** or bootcamp is a short intensive program for induction of recruits into an [army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army "Army") or [navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy "Navy"). In the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") a few military bases have special units devoted to basic training. The [jargon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jargon "Jargon") of the service is introduced as well as the fundamentals of military discipline and the recruits are trained in the basic skills of their service. A great deal of emphasis is placed on proper wearing of the uniform, grooming, and drill.

Army recruits are often instructed in the firing and care of [guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun "Gun"); Navy recruits get a short introduction to [fire fighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire_fighting "Fire fighting").

See [saltpetre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saltpetre "Saltpetre")

### Federation Cup

Main article: [Federation Cup (India)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_Cup_(India) "Federation Cup (India)")

East Bengal started the Federation Cup campaign in the Pre-Quarter Finals against [Air India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_India_F.C. "Air India F.C.") and won 3–1 with goals from Sydney Nkalanga, [Dipankar Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dipankar_Roy "Dipankar Roy") and [Mike Okoro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Okoro "Mike Okoro"). [Syed Rahim Nabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syed_Rahim_Nabi "Syed Rahim Nabi") scored an own-goal in the dying minutes to give consolation to Air India.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_East_Bengal_F.C._season#cite_note-4) In the quarter-final, however, East Bengal lost to [Churchill Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Churchill_Brothers_S.C. "Churchill Brothers S.C.") in the sudden-death after the game ended 0–0 after 120 minutes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_East_Bengal_F.C._season#cite_note-5)

### Federation Cup

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005%E2%80%9306_East_Bengal_FC_season&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Federation Cup")]

Main article: [Federation Cup (India)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_Cup_(India) "Federation Cup (India)")

East Bengal started the Federation Cup campaign in the Pre-Quarter Finals against [Air India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_India_F.C. "Air India F.C.") and won 3–1 with goals from Sydney Nkalanga, [Dipankar Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dipankar_Roy "Dipankar Roy") and [Mike Okoro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Okoro "Mike Okoro"). [Syed Rahim Nabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syed_Rahim_Nabi "Syed Rahim Nabi") scored an own-goal in the dying minutes to give consolation to Air India.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_East_Bengal_F.C._season#cite_note-4) In the quarter-final, however, East Bengal lost to [Churchill Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Churchill_Brothers_S.C. "Churchill Brothers S.C.") in the sudden-death after the game ended 0–0 after 120 minutes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_East_Bengal_F.C._season#cite_note-5)

**Alvito Ronaldo Correia D'Cunha** (born 12 July 1978, in [Sanvordem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanvordem "Sanvordem")) is a retired [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India")[football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_(soccer) "Football (soccer)") player. He was a former member of the [India national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_national_football_team "India national football team") and represented India in the [2002 FIFA World Cup qualifiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup "2002 FIFA World Cup"). He spent most of his club career in East Bengal.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alvito_D'Cunha#cite_note-2)

## Playing career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alvito_D%27Cunha&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Playing career")]

He played for [East Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SC_East_Bengal "SC East Bengal") as a left winger for a long span of 14 seasons. He retired at the start of 2016 season as the club had not included D'Cunha in the squad. He previously played for two renowned Goan sides [Salgaocar SC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salgaocar_SC "Salgaocar SC") (1998–2002), and [Sesa SC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sesa_Football_Academy "Sesa Football Academy") (1997–1998).

He made a start after a few years for East Bengal against [Kalighat Milan Sangha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalighat_Milan_Sangha_FC "Kalighat Milan Sangha FC") in the inaugural match of the Calcutta Premier Division 2013, where he scored from a penalty on the 15th minute, and assisted his state-mate [Joaquim Abranches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joaquim_Abranches "Joaquim Abranches") with a forward through pass to score his first goal for the [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata")-based side.

**Alvito Ronaldo Correia D'Cunha** (born 12 July 1978, in [Sanvordem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanvordem "Sanvordem")) is a retired [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India")[football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_(soccer) "Football (soccer)") player. He was a former member of the [India national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_national_football_team "India national football team") and represented India in the [2002 FIFA World Cup qualifiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup "2002 FIFA World Cup"). He spent most of his club career in East Bengal.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alvito_D'Cunha#cite_note-2)

## Playing career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alvito_D%27Cunha&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Playing career")]

He played for [East Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SC_East_Bengal "SC East Bengal") as a left winger for a long span of 14 seasons. He retired at the start of 2016 season as the club had not included D'Cunha in the squad. He previously played for two renowned Goan sides [Salgaocar SC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salgaocar_SC "Salgaocar SC") (1998–2002), and [Sesa SC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sesa_Football_Academy "Sesa Football Academy") (1997–1998).

He made a start after a few years for East Bengal against [Kalighat Milan Sangha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalighat_Milan_Sangha_FC "Kalighat Milan Sangha FC") in the inaugural match of the Calcutta Premier Division 2013, where he scored from a penalty on the 15th minute, and assisted his state-mate [Joaquim Abranches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joaquim_Abranches "Joaquim Abranches") with a forward through pass to score his first goal for the [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata")-based side.

Location of the two teams in [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata"), as well as [Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivekananda_Yuba_Bharati_Krirangan "Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan"), the shared home ground of the two clubs.

The **Kolkata Derby** (locally known as "Boro Match" i.e. "Big Match") is the [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") match in [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata"), between [Mohun Bagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohun_Bagan_Super_Giant "Mohun Bagan Super Giant") and [East Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Bengal_FC "East Bengal FC").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-7) The rivalry between these two teams dates back to over a century, and the matches witnessed large audience attendance and rivalry between patrons. It is considered to be the biggest Asian footballing rivalry. The first match was played on 8 August 1921 in [Cooch Behar Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooch_Behar_Cup "Cooch Behar Cup"). The Kolkata Derby is considered to be greatest derby in [Asian Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football_in_Asia "Association football in Asia") and also one of the [biggest derbies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_sports_rivalries "List of sports rivalries") in the world.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-8)

The two clubs meet at least three times a year, twice in the [Indian Super League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Super_League "Indian Super League") and once in the [Calcutta Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta_Football_League "Calcutta Football League"). Often these two clubs met in other competitions like the [Durand Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durand_Cup "Durand Cup"), [IFA Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFA_Shield "IFA Shield") and [Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Cup_(India) "Super Cup (India)").

Both clubs have large and dedicated fan bases around the world, and represent specific sections of [Bengali people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengalis "Bengalis"), Mohun Bagan represents people of [western part](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bengal "West Bengal") of [Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal "Bengal") (known as _[Ghotis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghoti\_people "Ghoti people")_), while East Bengal represents people from [eastern part](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Bengal "East Bengal") of pre-independence [Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal "Bengal") (known as _[Bangals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangal "Bangal")_). Culturally, this derby is similar to the [Scottish Professional Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Professional_Football_League "Scottish Professional Football League")'s [Old Firm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Firm "Old Firm") derby, since the Mohun Bagan supporters represent the 'nativist' population of [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India") Bengalis' (similar to [Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangers_F.C. "Rangers F.C.")) and the East Bengal fans represent the 'immigrant' population coming from [Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh "Bangladesh") (similar to [Celtic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_F.C. "Celtic F.C.")).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-10) The celebrations of a derby win is traditionally marked with dishes prepared from either _[ilish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilish "Ilish")_ or [_golda chingri_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macrobrachium_rosenbergii "Macrobrachium rosenbergii"), depending on which team wins.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-11) The East Bengal supporters celebrate their win with _ilish_ courses, being associated to the eastern region of Bengal (now [Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh "Bangladesh")), where as the Mohun Bagan fans celebrate with courses of _golda chingri_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-14)

## Origins

Further information: [Football in Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_in_Kolkata "Football in Kolkata")

Mohun Bagan is one of the oldest existing club of India having been established in 1889 in the city, then known under its anglicized name, Calcutta and till date one of the two most successful clubs in India, the other being East Bengal. The significant British influence in what was, until 1911, the nation's capital, ensured the game flourished, drawing players from other regions, and it is against this backdrop in which today's rivalry took root.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-15)

In 1920, the Jora Bagan club took field against Mohun Bagan who chose play without their star halfback Sailesh Bose, much to the chagrin of club vice-president Suresh Chandra Chaudhuri.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-16) Such was the industrialist's displeasure, he decided to form a new club and East Bengal was born. As Chaudhuri and his co-founders hailed from eastern part of Bengal, essentially now modern-day Bangladesh, the club became an identity for the people who migrated from that region during the [partition of Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_Bengal_(1905) "Partition of Bengal (1905)"). This resulted in the clubs being backed by two different socioeconomic groups, although this has largely changed over period of time. The first ever clash happened on **8 August 1921** in Cooch Behar Cup semifinal which ended in a goalless draw. Mohun Bagan would win the following replayed match on **10 August 1921** by defeating East Bengal **3–0**, courtesy to the goals from Rabi Ganguly, Poltu Dasgupta and Abhilash Ghosh. But the first official meeting is considered to be the CFL match-up held on **28 May 1925** at the Calcutta Football Ground (now [Mohun Bagan Ground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohun_Bagan_Ground "Mohun Bagan Ground")) where East Bengal won **1–0** with the help of a solitary goal from Nepal Chakraborty.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-20)

As of 2026, it is believed that the tally of overall meetings stands at **411** matches up till now, where **East Bengal** have been triumphant **145** and **Mohun Bagan****135 times** and **131 ended in draw**, which also includes walkover wins.

Among these two historic clubs, **Mohun Bagan** has won a total of **198** tournaments, while **East Bengal** has won **163** tournaments.

## History

[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/First_official_Kolkata_Derby_news_report.jpg/250px-First_official_Kolkata_Derby_news_report.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:First_official_Kolkata_Derby_news_report.jpg)

_News report, by [The Statesman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Statesman\_(India) "The Statesman (India)"), of first official Kolkata Derby, that took place on 28 May 1925._

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/11_August_1921_Kolkata_Derby_news_report.jpg/250px-11_August_1921_Kolkata_Derby_news_report.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:11_August_1921_Kolkata_Derby_news_report.jpg)

_News report, by The Statesman, of second Kolkata Derby, that took place on 10 August 1921, which was the replayed semi-final of Cooch Behar Cup after it went into a goalless draw the first time._

The first match between the sides was played on **8 August 1921** in the Coochbehar Cup, and the semifinal match ended in a 0–0 draw. Mohun Bagan won the replayed semifinal **3–0** on **10 August 1921** which was the first-ever win in this historic derby.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-21) Rabi Ganguly scored the first-ever derby goal in that match, and the other two goals were scored by Poltu Dasgupta and Abhilash Ghosh.

The first official match between the sides was played on **28 May 1925** in [CFL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta_Football_League "Calcutta Football League"), where East Bengal beat Mohun Bagan **1–0** with the help of a solitary goal from Nepal Chakraborty.

Mohun Bagan holds the record of scoring the fastest goal in a derby _(24 July 1976, a **17-second** goal from **Md Akbar** of Mohun Bagan)_. They have the record of winning two consecutive derbies on two successive days _(7 and 8 August 1935)_ and had the unique distinction of losing only one derby in **7** years _(**1933 to 1939**)_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-22)_During this phase, they won **29** trophies. Out of 23 derbies they won **12**, drew 10 and lost only 1 against their arch-rivals. It was a golden period in the history of the club_.

A few notable victories include the Darbhanga Shield match on 5 September 1934, when Mohun Bagan won **4–1**_([Amiya Deb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amiya\_Deb "Amiya Deb") scored all four goals)_. Another memorable instance where they scored four goals against was in Raja Memorial Shield final played on **6 August 1937** at the common ground of both the clubs ([Eden Gardens Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Gardens "Eden Gardens")), where Mohun Bagan beat East Bengal **4–0** and Asit Ganguly scored three goals in that match.

The 1960s proved a golden period for Mohun Bagan and it concluded in perfect fashion for the Mariners. Having already won the league, Mohun Bagan then did the double, defeating their rivals on their own ground in the IFA Shield final. The **3–1** victory credited to the then revolutionary 4–2–4 formation employed by innovative coach [Amal Dutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amal_Dutta "Amal Dutta").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-24)

The wheel eventually turned, and the 1970s was East Bengal's decade.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-25) The Red and Gold Brigade remained undefeated in the Derbies for 1932 days.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-26) In fact, they lost only one derby (that too outside Kolkata) in six years (1970 to 1975) which culminated in a **5–0** IFA Shield win over their great rivals. The Red and Golds won with a record 5–0 scoreline and, with it, a record of five consecutive Shield victories. Such was the ignominy surrounding the heavy defeat that several Mohun Bagan players spent the night holed up on a boat in the [Ganges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganges "Ganges") trying to escape the wrath of shell-shocked supporters.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-27) Umakanto Palodhi, an ardent Mohun Bagan fan, committed suicide. He wrote in his suicide note that in his next life he will born as a Mohun Bagan footballer and will take revenge of that 0–5 defeat.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-28)

On 16 August 1980, 16 football fans died due to stampede and riot inside the [Eden Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Gardens "Eden Gardens") stadium, Kolkata on the occasion of a Kolkata Derby match in the Calcutta Football League.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-goal.com-29)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-30) It is now remembered as [Football Lover's Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_Lover's_Day "Football Lover's Day").

The most memorable derby on many accounts took place in 1997 at the [semi-final of the Federation Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Bengal_4%E2%80%931_Mohun_Bagan "East Bengal 4–1 Mohun Bagan"), when a remarkable crowd of **1,31,781**[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-31) – a record attendance for any sport in India – filled a heaving [Salt Lake Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_Stadium "Salt Lake Stadium"). India's most recognizable footballer, [Baichung Bhutia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baichung_Bhutia "Baichung Bhutia"), took centre stage, scoring a hat-trick as East Bengal triumphed **4–1**.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-ie1-32)

On 25 October 2009, Mohun Bagan beat East Bengal **5–3** with [Chidi Edeh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chidi_Edeh "Chidi Edeh") scoring a hat-trick for Bagan _(4 goals)_ in an [I-League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I-League "I-League") encounter.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-33)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-auto-6)

On 6 September 2015, another memorable derby took place when East Bengal FC equaled the record for the highest margin of victory in a Calcutta Football League Derby as they triumphed 4–0 against Mohun Bagan. South Korean forward [Do Dong-hyun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do_Dong-hyun "Do Dong-hyun") scored a free-kick brace while [Mohammed Rafique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammed_Rafique_(footballer) "Mohammed Rafique (footballer)") and [Rahul Bheke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahul_Bheke "Rahul Bheke") scored the other two as the Red and Gold brigade matched their own record which they set back on 23 May 1936, when they defeated the Green and Maroons by the similar 4–0 scoreline with goals from Laxminarayan, K. Prasad, Murgesh and Majid.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-35)

On 29 January 2022, in an ISL derby Mohun Bagan beat East Bengal **3–1** scores with a hat-trick from [Kiyan Nassiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiyan_Nassiri "Kiyan Nassiri"), son of former East Bengal player [Jamshid Nassiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamshid_Nassiri "Jamshid Nassiri"), and became the youngest player to score a hat-trick in the derby.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-36) East Bengal lost six consecutive derbies since 2019.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

On 25 February 2023, Mohun Bagan made the record of winning back to back **eight consecutive derbies**— one in the [Durand Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durand_Cup "Durand Cup"), one in the [I-League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I-League "I-League") and six in the [ISL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Super_League "Indian Super League")_(From 19 January 2020)_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The derby of [2025–26 Indian Super League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_Indian_Super_League "2025–26 Indian Super League") on 17 May 2026 became the most consequential derby in the history of the first tier league due to the direct title implications it carried in the season.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-37) The match ended in a 1—1 draw with both goals scored within the last five minutes.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Derby#cite_note-ISL_26_derby-38)
